George Russell is among the drivers who isn’t using one, which is interesting a) because Russell has suffered badly from heat in the past (Qatar, Singapore) and b) because he states Mercedes chose to put the development money into car upgrades instead.

Recent findings suggest that it’s an interesting admission. Not everyone is sold on the idea of cooling vests. Ferrari and McLaren will definitely be using them this weekend, for instance. Max Verstappen won’t as he doesn’t like them. Russell thinks the FIA should just develop the tech themselves and it shouldn’t be part of the budget cap.

According to recent reports, “Our team have put a lot of emphasis this year on the cockpit temperature,” he said. “We won’t be running the cooling vest because we haven’t put the resource into making it robust enough. I feel we need the FIA just to step in and say ‘Here’s some money extra in the cost cap or there’s an external company who’s going to develop it for everybody’. Because we should all be wearing it. When it works, it works great. So, I would like to wear it this week, and I would like to wear it next week. But the team asked me...look, we can develop it, and we can put the money towards it...[but at a cost].

He added: “The top itself is not expensive ..you’ve got to effectively make a system where you can fit a block of dry ice or actual ice, and then has the airflow to circulate the cool water throughout. If that system isn’t robust enough, then suddenly you have no circulation, and then you get hot. You get ambient temperature circulating. The vest is one-design, but the system that circulates the water is different [at different teams].”.

The two Ferraris are on medium tyres but Leclerc still puts himself into second place. He is then displaced by Hamilton, who slots in behind Verstappen. Good times from the Ferraris on the mediums.

What about the McLarens? Norris goes sixth fastest but is more than six tenths down on Verstappen. Then comes Piastri, who goes fourth fastest, just under four tenths off Verstappen.

Arguably the three favourites for pole; Antonelli, Russell and Verstappen, are all on flying laps.

The first sector goes the way of Verstappen, who is purple, and then the Dutchman goes purple in the middle sector.

According to recent reports, antonelli is two tenths faster than his teammate Russell but Verstappen is over half a second quicker than the Mercedes. Hadjar is then second fastest to show the pace in the Red Bull this weekend.

It has been revealed that most of the teams waited and waited to come out and then suddenly lots of drivers are sent out, resulting in a queue in the pits! With the high track temperatures and high degradation, the drivers are crawling around on their out laps to preserve these soft tyres.

Recent findings suggest that bumper to bumper in the pit lane! #F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/ff8JO9kB1g.

The two Haas drivers have a free track to themselves whilst everyone else bides their time. In theory, as the hour of qualifying goes on, the track temperature should decrease and the more rubber that is laid down the faster the track should get.

Finally, just before the two Haas drivers finish their first flying laps, the rest of the grid is starting to emerge, led by the Mercedes duo.

The green light is showing at the end of the pit lane and Q1 is officially under way. The two Haas drivers are the first to head out. Other than that, it is a quiet start to Q1.

The top four teams; Mercedes, Red Bull, Ferrari and McLaren, all have a genuine chance of taking pole in Sepang today. I think the true favourites though have to be the Mercedes duo and Max Verstappen but with how close it between all four of the teams you cannot rule anything out.

It is 33 degrees celsius air temperature, with the track temperature up at 58 degrees.

According to recent reports, not long to wait now until qualifying begins. It is hot, humid and dry in Sepang right now. As we know in Malaysia, the weather can change quickly and thunderstorms can roll in quite quickly but it looks like today’s qualifying will be a dry one. This will be one of if not the hottest qualifying sessions of the season, so much so that we are seeing umbrellas going up to get some shade from the sun rather than sheltering from any rain.

This will be important to consider after qualifying finishes as there will be some shuffling around:.

Isack Hadjar (Red Bull): five-place grid penalty- new internal combustion engineFranco Colapinto (Alpine): ten-place grid penalty- new engineFranco Colapinto (Alpine): five-place grid penalty- causing a collision in BakuArvid Lindblad (Racing Bulls): back of the grid- complete power unit change.

According to recent reports, hadjar has looked good since returning from his wrist injury so could be fighting it out near the front of the grid, although his five-place penalty will drop him down. We know Lindblad will be at the back and is very likely to be joined there by Colapinto, who is not going to be qualifying high up in the top ten in his Alpine.

Industry observers note that haas have revealed that Frenchman Esteban Ocon will leave at the end of this season. Ocon now faces an uncertain future, with it difficult to see a spot for him on the F1 grid next season. There are suggestions that the 30-year-old’s replacement will be Brazilian Ferrari junior Rafael Camara, although nothing has been confirmed on that front. 21-year-old Camara presently leads the Formula 2 championship.

TGR Haas F1 Team and Esteban Ocon will part ways at the conclusion of the 2026 season. With plenty of racing ahead, our focus remains on working together to maximize every opportunity through to the final race of the year.#HaasF1 #F1 pic.twitter.com/4iQAuqnSyA.

Industry observers note that aston Martin have now confirmed their driver line-up for next season, retaining both Fernando Alonso and Lance Stroll. There had been reports that Alonso had been contemplating retirement but the 45-year-old will continue into another season.

Aston Martin Aramco confirms Lance and Fernando will continue as the team's drivers in 2027. Read more: ​https://t.co/ePyjJdyAIB pic.twitter.com/VogFUEbNxy.

Other than the second seat alongside Ollie Bearman at Haas, the only other team to keep an eye on is Racing Bulls, with no definite confirmation on their exact driver line-up for next season.

Ferrari this week have publicly backed their team principal Frederic Vasseur, amid speculation over the Frenchman’s position and comments made by former Red Bull team principal Christian Horner, who said the job at Ferrari would be a “dream job”. Ferrari, who sit second in the constructors’ standings, have not won the drivers’ championship since 2007 (Kimi Raikkonen) and the constructors’ since 2008. Here is a snippet from Tom Cary’s piece on the matter:.

In a hastily convened media call on Tuesday morning, Maria Conti, Ferrari’s chief communication officer, said the Scuderia had decided to issue a vote of confidence in Vasseur in response “not just to the story of Mr Horner, but in general, the speculation about Fred”.

“Ferrari has made its choices,” Conti remarked. “We have confidence – full confidence – in Fred Vasseur and in his team, and we continue to do so.

“At this time, it’s really important that the team remains united and cohesive, and we are focused with all the energy on the work ahead.”.

According to recent reports, “It is great to be back [in Malaysia]. I am really enjoying the track. We have had some wonderful races here over time. It is actually the 20th time we have been here, it started in 1999, and it is really exciting to be back. I really enjoyed getting out on the track and watching the cars closely.

Industry observers note that “The drivers are super fit and they have some cooling but it is not easy. But you almost cannot get enough fluid through your body before your stomach gives up. Having this race and Singapore back-to-back increases that challenge.”.

Especially with the major upgrade they have brought this weekend, Mercedes’ lead at the summit is looking unassailable right now.

Almost nine years ago to the day, Max Verstappen took just his second race victory in Formula 1. Lewis Hamilton, who took pole position, and Daniel Ricciardo joined Verstappen on the podium. Despite being nine years ago, plenty of drivers still on the grid were racing that weekend. Here they are and who they were racing for:.

Max Verstappen (Red Bull) Lewis Hamilton (Mercedes) Valtteri Bottas (Mercedes) Esteban Ocon (Force India)Nico Hulkenberg (Renault)Sergio Perez (Force India)Fernando Alonso (McLaren)Lance Stroll (Williams)Carlos Sainz (Toro Rosso)Pierre Gasly (Toro Rosso).

Sources indicate that with Russell winning in Baku and Antonelli finishing fifth, the latter’s championship lead was cut to 66 points. If Russell is going to usurp his teammate, he is going to need a few more similar results to last weekend due to the size of Antonelli’s lead. If Antonelli were to suffer a retirement, then that completely changes the outlook.

It has been revealed that formula One returns to Malaysia for round 16 of the season for the Bahrain Grand Prix. That probably sounds strange but after the Bahrain Grand Prix was originally postponed in March, F1 reinstated it to the calendar with Malaysia hosting it because of the ongoing war in the Middle East. Despite being held in Malaysia, Bahrain have retained the naming rights for the event, which is officially known as the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia. The last time Formula One was in Malaysia was nine years ago back in 2017, when a young whippersnapper named Max Verstappen, still four years away from winning his first world championship, claimed just his second victory.

Last time out around the streets of Baku, Mercedes’ George Russell claimed victory at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, pipping Verstappen by just a tenth of a second. That was Russell’s first grand prix win since June and cuts his team-mate Kimi Antonelli’s lead in the drivers’ standings to 66 points. Antonelli had a challenging weekend in Baku, starting 16th after a crash in qualifying and coming home in fifth to see his championship lead to Russell cut by 15 points.

Verstappen was quickest in first practice yesterday, with the Ferrari of Charles Leclerc fastest in second practice. Earlier today, championship leader Antonelli was nearly three tenths clear of the field in third practice. Mercedes, 160 points clear at the top of the constructors’ standings, have brought significant upgrades this weekend, which includes a new floor, rear suspension and rear corner. It is the team’s first significant car upgrade since the Canadian Grand at the end of May.

It has been revealed that this race in Malaysia represents the second leg of the season’s first flyaway triple header, with the Singapore Grand Prix to come next weekend, so the demands on the teams and the drivers are incredibly high. Qualifying from Sepang gets under way at 9am (GMT).

Germany hopes to host world ice hockey championship — without Russia

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that since the October 30 decision, several leading ice hockey nations — including Finland, Sweden and Czechia — have stated they would refrain from playing against Russia in any tournament in which it is allowed to take part.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A government spokesman has remarked that, despite talks with the German Ice Hockey Federation (DEB), the International Ice Hockey Federation (DEB) and others, the impasse caused by last week's Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) ruling remains.

Industry observers note that since the October 30 decision, several leading ice hockey nations — including Finland, Sweden and Czechia — have stated they would refrain from playing against Russia in any tournament in which it is allowed to take part. Several key sponsors have also threatened to pull out, should the Russians be allowed to play.

The first tournament to be affected would be the Men's World Juniors, which opens in Canada in late December, followed by the IIHF's premier event, the Men's World Ice Championship, to be hosted by Germany in May.

Stefan Kornelius, the spokesman for Germany's government, told reporters in Berlin on Friday that talks held with various stakeholders had made clear that Russia's participation would render the hosting of the championship "practically impossible — both from a sporting and an economic perspective.".

Kornelius said talks would continue and the government still hoped for a diplomatic solution that would allow Germany to host the championship — as planned — in Gelsenkirchen, Mannheim and Düsseldorf in May.

"Our goal must be to hold the tournaments as scheduled," he said. "However, given the boycotts that would follow Russia's readmission, that would effectively be impossible. For this reason, we intend to explore — through dialogue — how we can still ensure the tournament takes place.".

Following the CAS ruling that the IIHF must allow Russia to return to international play, DEB chairman Frank Lutz had conceded that Germany may be forced to consider withdrawing as championship host.

Asked at Friday's press conference whether Germany could issue visas to a Russian team for the tournament, a Foreign Ministry spokesman declined to answer categorically, but did indicate that this would be difficult under restrictions at the moment in place.

"At a time when Russia is waging a war of aggression against Ukraine, there can be no 'normalcy' — and we will certainly not pretend that there is," said spokesperson Martin Giese.

Earlier this week, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney categorically ruled out Russian players taking part in the World Juniors in Alberta.

"While Russia and Belarus are supporting this illegal, unjustified ​war in Ukraine, as long as that's going on, there will be none of those athletes competing for their countries in Canada," he said.

"So, ​if you're asking specifically about the World Juniors," he said, "the Russians will not be there.".

Russian President Vladimir Putin has also weighed in on the matter, accusing countries opposing Russia's return to international sport of violating the rights of his country's athletes.

The IIHF Council had originally called two days of meetings, on Monday and Tuesday, to try to reach a consensus on how to respond to the CAS decision — before extending discussions for a third day, on Thursday. By Friday, its members had evidently still not reached a consensus.

This comes as the Women's Ice Hockey World Championship, which is not affected by the CAS decision, opened in Denmark — and with the clock ticking toward the start of the World Juniors in Alberta on December 26.

A valuable success for the Azzurri, who put an end to a series of disappointing results in the league and can regain some confidence before the rest of the season. Three of Everton's Premier League fixtures in January – including the Merseyside derby at Anfield – have been moved for live television coverage.

The Toffees' trip to Coventry City remains on Saturday 16 January, but with an earlier kick-off time of 12.30pm (GMT), and will be shown live on TNT Sports.

The following weekend, David Moyes' side will now host Brentford at Hill Dickinson Stadium on Sunday 24 January, in a 2pm (GMT) kick-off that will be broadcast live on Sky Sports.

Finally, the Merseyside derby against Liverpool at Anfield on Saturday 30 January will now take place at the earlier time of 12.30pm (GMT) and will be live on TNT Sports.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If this is Tuchel-ball, if this is the way Thomas Tuchel wants England to play, then yes, please. More of the same; bring it on. The standard is set.

England’s DNA? This was a total-football annihilation of a top nation. Croatia, 14th in the world and fierce competitors, were cowed and humiliated at home in this Nations League tie. This was the biggest defeat in their proud history – seventh heaven for England, and hell for the hosts.

Sources indicate that the visitors were sublime. Harry Kane (twice – 89 goals now for his country), Jude Bellingham and Anthony Gordon all scored and were outstanding. Bukayo Saka also struck twice. Alex Scott made his first start and will take some dislodging. The Bournemouth midfielder was slick with a snap – perpetual, intelligent, smooth motion.

Harry Kane at the DOUBLE! 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿The Three Lions have FIVE in Rijeka 🦁 pic.twitter.com/BRnVXADtHC.

Luka Modric has had the most extraordinary career but he was emphatically second best here and was subbed off on 57 minutes at 5-0. He looked bereft, having had Scott and Elliot Anderson run all over him and Mateo Kovacic.

We came out of the World Cup wondering if Tuchel really had an idea of how he can get England over the line. After last Saturday’s defeat by world and European champions Spain, followed by Tuesday’s win over the Czech Republic we still did not know.

Recent findings suggest that but here the standard was set – it was an exhilarating example of the football England are capable of. On display we saw the speed, the movement, the passes under pressure, the ambition, the control and aggression. This was the full package. Bottle it. Bag it. Believe it.

According to recent reports, croatia have an ageing team and are in transition, but they were left looking callow. It looked as though it was men against boys. There were plenty of boys in the stands, with 6,200 children allowed in for what was supposed to be a behind-closed-doors fixture – Croatia’s punishment for crowd trouble.

Their new head coach Slaven Bilic would doubtless have been relieved that the match was not played in front of the usual, passionate, partisan crowd. Even then some of the kids booed and left early. Bilic looked shell-shocked. As well he might.

Sources indicate that and Saka makes it FOUR! ⚽️⚽️⚽️⚽️England break to devastating effect - Croatia are reeling... pic.twitter.com/60EgNt4cfh.

Sources indicate that it was 4-0 at half-time. It could easily have been 7-1 – Kovacic missed a sitter for Croatia at 3-0 and Gordon should have had a hat-trick. How significant is it that England’s three most dangerous players do not play in the Premier League? Probably not very. But the fact they turn out for Real Madrid, Barcelona and Bayern Munich is. They performed like the top players their clubs think they clearly are.

Gordon heads in to make it THREE! 💥England are cruising 🛳️ pic.twitter.com/nqwUxFmkof.

Recent findings suggest that kane’s commitment was incredible. At one stage Croatia substitute Kristijan Jakić threatened to break clear but was stopped by England’s last man tracking back. It was Kane, one cap short of equalling Peter Shilton’s all-time record of 125 appearances, and it was already 5-0 when that happened.

These could be exciting times for England. Times when they have shaken off the debate over how well or otherwise they did at the World Cup and moved on. Tuchel has talked up that third-place finish; we have tended to dwell on the semi-final exit to Argentina.

And now? If Tuchel does go and win a trophy for England, he will be talking about this game. Previously he referenced the 5-0 demolition of Serbia in Belgrade, during the World Cup qualification. But the Serbians were a rabble. Croatia are not, but were made to look so on Saturday.

According to recent reports, where will this sit among England performances? There was the 2-1 victory away to Italy at the beginning of the Euro 2024 qualification campaign in March 2023. Before that, the 3-2 win away to Spain in 2018, also in the Nations League. But England were more thrilling here. Do we have to go back to 5-1 in Munich in 2001?

Industry observers note that the concern will be the familiar England problem of looking like world-beaters in the autumn and worn out by the time a tournament comes around in the summer. But against Croatia there was control and authority as they raised their chances of finishing in the top two and qualifying for next March’s quarter-finals.

Industry observers note that the goals rained in – even if the best remained the first as Marc Guéhi intercepted a clearance, Scott took the ball on the half-turn and found Bellingham. He slid it through to Kane who finished high into the net. What a goal.

Recent findings suggest that bellingham ➡️ Kane! ⚽️The Three Lions lead in Rijeka with their first shot on target 🎯 pic.twitter.com/ZLcnGLvj3z.

Recent findings suggest that england were swarming all over Croatia. Saka crossed, Gordon took the ball down and turned it back for Bellingham to stab home.

What a touch from Anthony Gordon! 🔥The Barca man squares it to the Real Madrid man and England lead 2-0 ⚽️⚽️ pic.twitter.com/31Y1Ojx44M.

According to recent reports, gordon, after twice being denied, got his goal – with another header, as against the Czechs. This time Jarell Quansah, back in ahead of Trent Alexander-Arnold, delivered from the right and Gordon met it to score for the fourth successive game for England. Even before half-time England were not finished as Bellingham crossed low from the left and found Saka, who found the back of the net.

After the break, the hunger remained insatiable. Anderson was sent down the right and Kane slid in. Croatia then lost the ball sloppily inside their own area, Kane thought about shooting but unselfishly fed Saka, who claimed a second goal.

According to recent reports, saka should have had a hat-trick before substitute Morgan Rogers wrapped up the scoring, collecting a ball over the top from the relentless Bellingham – once again captain after Kane went off – and finishing with ease after rounding the goalkeeper. It was a third assist for Bellingham and a seventh goal for England. It could have been double figures.

Absolutely [that was the 90-minute performance we’ve been looking for]. Maybe three minutes after the three-zero there was a major mistake [Kovacic’s chance] and some easy ball losses but that was a performance of the highest level from everyone. And from the first until the last minute from everyone who started and everyone who came on. Congratulations to the team.

Very, very impressive [to do this] on an away pitch. We created so many chances in the first 40 minutes. We were so fluid from the start. I looked at the clock and thought ‘Oh, this has been a good three minutes, this has been a good seven minutes…’ and it never stopped.

We kept the pace up and played through the gaps, stayed hungry in our counter-pressing and defending.

We played humble and always got the basics right.

Unbelievable from start to finish. We spoke a lot about having a 90-minute game in which we were dominant with and without the ball and that was it out there. We’re at our best when we’re brave and we’re physically overpowering. When we make it a Premier League game and they couldn’t live with our pace, our movement, our runs. And we were clinical.

There’s freedom. All four of us [him, Bellingham, Saka and Gordon] can play in the 10 pocket, play as the nine. I can play as a midfielder. We’re good enough and smart enough so if we lose the ball we can cover in midfield and defence. That’s the way we want to play. It’s so hard for them to pick a man and press. Every man was at the highest level.

Beautiful hotel, lovely weather, we could easily have fallen into that holiday mode. It’s an unusual situation for us. We’ve never been away this long in this kind of camp and that’s the perfect end to the week,.

Sources indicate that [And now to equal Peter Shilton’s record 125th cap on Tuesday?] That would be nice. That’s why he keeps taking me off, to rest me for the next game. That’s what he mentioned to me after. I’ll be ready to start on Tuesday.

An amazing night for us. We came out from the start on top and played with high energy and we punished them.

It was special and fun to play. We were really clinical today. Two goals for England is always a nice feeling.

We revealed the hunger, passion and quality we had. A mixture of everything we wanted to show.

Recent findings suggest that [Bellingham] was amazing tonight. He deserved man of the match and deserves to be player of the year.

At least the Croatia fans did not seem too dispirited, the kids smiling and waving at the camera, despite the utter trouncing their team took.

England were terrific but how much of that was because Croatia were terrible will be open to debate.

Scott has come in for Myles Lewis-Skelly in what looks to be an attacking change from Tuchel, the England head coach.

Jordan Pickford has revealed he spends up to three hours talking to a “mindwork coach”.

The England goalkeeper has worked with sports psychologists for some time but has gone into detail about how committed he is as he faces a challenge to his No 1 spot from James Trafford.

Pickford will start for England in the Nations League tie against Croatia, and next Tuesday’s fixture at home to the Czech Republic, having missed out on the past two games.

Trafford was in goal for the 3-2 loss to Spain and the 2-0 victory away to the Czechs and although Thomas Tuchel has stated Pickford remains his first choice it is known that he and his coaching staff are huge admirers of Leeds United’s fresh goalkeeper.

Trent Alexander-Arnold is expected to drop back down to the substitutes’ bench for England’s third Nations League game against Croatia in Rijeka.

Despite Alexander-Arnold providing an assist for Anthony Gordon against the Czech Republic, England head coach Thomas Tuchel is expected to replace him with Jarell Quansah at right-back.

Sources indicate that jude Bellingham is also in line for a recall, most likely in place of Morgan Rogers, while Tuchel had been hopeful of Ezri Konsa returning to fitness to replace Trevoh Chalobah in the centre of defence. Goalkeeper Jordan Pickford replaces James Trafford.

Sources indicate that uefa fined the Croatian football federation £80,000 and ordered them to play their next Uefa-sanctioned home match behind closed doors because of their fans’ racist chanting and for fireworks offences during a Nations League match against France in 2025. Croatia have played Fifa-sanctioned World Cup qualifiers and friendlies at home in front of fans since but tonight is the first in Uefa competition and hence the ban.

However, a caveat in Uefa’s disciplinary regulations allows the home federation in such circumstances to fill the ground to 75 per cent of its capacity with “children up to the age of 14 (duly accompanied) from schools and/or football academies invited to the match free of charge”. And given the scrum outside the stadium this afternoon, that is what is happening.

Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of England’s Uefa Nations League Group A3 match against Croatia in Rijeka. Matches between the two are relatively frequent – 12 in 30 years. Croatia have beaten England three times in the 10 competitive meetings, home and away in qualification for Euro 2008, which dealt the England manager a blow from which he could not recover, and the World Cup semi-final in Moscow in 2018.

The extraordinary thing about both the first two defeats – the ‘Wally with the Brolly’ match in November 2007, Steve McLaren’s last in charge, and the home tie on October 10 2006 – is that Luka Modric played in both. And now eight days shy of 20 years since his first appearance against England, he is still running their midfield at the age of 41.

England have had the upper hand since Russia, winning in the Nations League at Wembley in 2018, opening their Euro 2020 campaign with a 1-0 victory by virtue of Raheem Sterling’s goal and then in June when they were at their fluent best, a rare occurrence, in the second half of their first World Cup group game to push on from 2-2 to finish 4-2.

Slaven Bilic, manager from 2006-12, is back in charge for his second spell but his squad still relies heavily on experienced players. Modric is the eldest but is joined by greybeard stalwarts Ivan Perisic, Ante Budimir and Andrej Kramaric, both 35. Spain hammered them 4-1 in midweek after they had started with a 2-1 victory over Czech Republic in Prague.

England, who rattled Spain and should have gone 3-1 up but lost 3-2, were much better in the second half in Prague against a team reduced to 10 men and deserved their 2-0 win, have played at the tiny Stadion Rujevica (capacity 8,279) once before, drawing 0-0 in 2018.

Thomas Tuchel, who changed three of his back four on Tuesday, may stick with Lewis Hall after he made a positive impression in combination with Anthony Gordon. As for Trent Alexander-Arnold, who set up the first goal, Tuchel does not go out of his way to undermine the perception that for all his unique quality, he just doesn’t fancy the Real Madrid right-back at all.

It’s up to Alexander-Arnold to make a compelling case if picked today or at Wembley on Tuesday to persuade the German head coach not to restore his beloved if brittle ‘Reecey’ James at the first opportunity.

Luke McCowan's timely return to form silences Parkhead critics and boosts midfield options

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

Published: 11:58 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 12:18 EST, 22 November 2026.

Almost everyone who has played the game of football at a professional level has experienced a day where they simply can’t do right for doing wrong.

When one heavy touch leads to another and each decision made seems worse than the last one.

Like the buses in his native Greenock, it was Luke McCowan’s misfortune for two such traumatic experiences to arrive in close proximity.

His inept performance as a substitute on a dark night for Celtic in Linz in August will flash through his mind when he’s old and grey.

Handed the opportunity to atone for it with a start in the league game against Rangers at Parkhead the following month, his withdrawal at half-time felt like an act of mercy.

A Celtic supporter all his days, McCowan didn’t have to speak to articulate the depth of his despair in that trying time. Subjected to a barrage of online criticism, the deletion of his social media accounts mentioned enough.

Luke McCowan scored in the 4-1 home victory over St Mirren.

Skipper Callum McGregor and McCowan enjoy the victory at full-time.

While you could understand why the midfielder would have felt personally responsible for a pair of high-profile losses, there was a lot more to the team’s shortcomings on those occasions than one man performing as if his laces were tied together.

Away to LASK, Celtic were already wilting when he shed his tracksuit. He didn’t stop the slide towards an extraordinary exit from the Champions League but he didn’t instigate it.

At home to Rangers, Celtic were flat and second-best from the outset and remained that way even after McCowan came inside for the second period.

In a recent development, the 28-year-old was not alone in failing to do himself justice on those occasions and in other matches around what was a difficult period for Martin O’Neill’s side. It might just have felt like it.

As shown by his contributions to a side who were capable of winning the title in his first two seasons in Glasgow, McCowan was – and is – a far more accomplished player than those unfortunate episodes suggested.

According to recent reports, he wasn’t the first and he won’t be the last player to suffer a crisis of confidence. And despite being no shrinking violet, he would not be human if those experiences didn’t shake him up and lead him to question if he was worthy of wearing the jersey that he always dreamed of.

His display on Saturday should have emphatically answered those inner doubts.

Trusted by his manager to fill the void created by the injury to Mika Baur, McCowan delivered.

Industry observers note that even before he scored to put the game to bed just before half-time, he played smart passes, made intelligent runs and made key interceptions. He looked very much a Celtic player again.

McGregor takes the acclaim from team-mates after scoring Celtic's fourth goal.

No one in O’Neill’s side, in fact, did more to ensure that they went up the tunnel at the interval to warm applause.

With Baur’s absence for up to ten weeks already a source of stress to the Celtic manager, Benjamin Nygren’s sore heel would have further disrupted his sleep on Friday night.

Saturday proved to be quite the day for O’Neill’s fringe men, though.

On top of McCowan’s assured display, we witnessed Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain serve up a reminder of why he once wore the jerseys of Arsenal, Liverpool and England.

Sources indicate that playing deeper than McCowan, Oxlade-Chamberlain stretched St Mirren with his pinpoint passing, long and short. He kept the ball in tight areas and made it all look so simple.

He was in the right place at the right time to stroke home Yang Hyun-jun’s cut-back to put his side in front and never put a foot wrong until his legs could give no more.

The cherry on the cake for O’Neill came by way of Joel van den Berg’s debut from the bench.

Having seen the club shell out over £3million to PSV Eindhoven, Celtic supporters were growing a little concerned that the teenager hadn’t yet featured for the first team.

Now fully recovered from an injury, he belatedly caught the eye. Tall, skilful and rangy, he looked the part. Might he have earned himself a call-up to the Europa League squad as a replacement for Baur? You would not be surprised.

Celtic will certainly travel to Portugal to face Torreense on Thursday in optimistic mood after making short work of seeing off the Buddies.

According to recent reports, arriving just before McCowan turned home Kieran Tierney’s cross, Camilo Duran claimed his 14th of the season by bundling in a brilliant assist from the same source. Stationed on the bench throughout, Kasper Hogh wasn’t even afforded a chance to end his 16-game goal drought.

On a good day for a makeshift midfield, Callum McGregor, its mainstay, claimed Celtic’s fourth with a controlled strike after the break.

Sources indicate that sam Johnstone didn’t have a great deal to do, testament to Celtic’s work without the ball. Tierney was excellent for 71 minutes, despite playing the entirety of Scotland’s games with North Macedonia and Switzerland.

Recent findings suggest that the directness and industry of Yang on the right flank was also eye-catching. Omitted from the squad for the second successive match, Haissem Hassan will surely have taken note.

On the other flank, Jota looked like a player who’s threatening to really fire again.

A late run-out for Auston Trusty, the first since the death of his father, was met by warm applause by home fans. O’Neill will certainly need the American in the coming weeks.

While Killian Phillips did spoil Johnstone’s clean sheet by converting a penalty which the keeper gave away, O’Neill would have had few complaints about a display which saw his side create an abundance of opportunities.

Sources indicate that it must be mentioned that St Mirren were their own worst enemies. They are proving to be a strange fish under Craig McLeish. Even in defeat, some of their football on Saturday was eye-catching.

According to recent reports, yet again, though, they revealed themselves to be a soft touch defensively. They were fortunate not to ship more than four and it’s hardly a fresh thing, either.

Recent findings suggest that the Buddies haven’t kept a clean sheet since winning by a goal at Rugby Park on September 2. In the ten subsequent matches, they’ve picked the ball out of their net 23 times. It’s becoming a real concern.

While they are more creative and entertaining than when Stephen Robinson was in charge, they could badly do with becoming as hard to beat as they were under their former boss.

They are now just five points above Kilmarnock ahead of their meeting in Paisley this weekend. That would be an opportune moment for it all to come together.

ST MIRREN: (4-2-3-1) Chapman 5; Ramsay 5, Jackson 5, Gogic 5, John 4; Carr 6 (Donnelly 84), Nsio 5.5 (Taylor 85); Thomas 5 (Young 65), Phillips 5.5 (Ramos 74), Kabia 5; Sule 5 (Mochrie 65). Booked: Gogic. Manager: Craig McLeish 4.

#140295. As COP31 Antalya kicks off, can world move beyond significant promises?

📅 08 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1231 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dw ↗ Open Full Page

As COP31 Antalya kicks off, can world move beyond significant promises?

📅 08 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1231 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • With its pulsing music, flashy images and barrage of special effects, the key message in Antalya's marketing video is clear: Turkey, the host of the 31st edition of the UN climate talks, is cool, stylish, modern — and eco-conscious.
  • Both President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and his wife, Emine, make an appearance, with Turkey's first lady calling climate change "one of the most visible manifestations of the burden human activity has placed on our planet.".
  • Industry observers note that from November 9-20, delegates from nearly every country in the world are coming together in the Mediterranean city of Antalya to chart a way out of the climate crisis.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

With its pulsing music, flashy images and barrage of special effects, the key message in Antalya's marketing video is clear: Turkey, the host of the 31st edition of the UN climate talks, is cool, stylish, modern — and eco-conscious.

Both President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and his wife, Emine, make an appearance, with Turkey's first lady calling climate change "one of the most visible manifestations of the burden human activity has placed on our planet.".

Industry observers note that from November 9-20, delegates from nearly every country in the world are coming together in the Mediterranean city of Antalya to chart a way out of the climate crisis. Turkey is the official host, and Australia will lead the negotiations. But the concerns they'll confront during those 12 days are far more serious than the showy marketing campaign make them out to be.

Severe drought, extreme heat, wildfires and record-low water levels in Europe's main waterways — summer across the continent was dominated by climate emergencies.

Industry observers note that and in late August, a series of flash floods triggered by a rock-ice avalanche in Nepal and Tibet washed away entire villages, killing more than 1,400 people and leaving thousands missing. Climate experts have linked the disaster to melting ice and a warming climate.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Globally, carbon emissions are still rising: the UN has concluded that it is no longer possible to keep global temperature rise to 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 Fahrenheit) above pre-industrial levels, the goal agreed at COP21 in 2015.

Recent findings suggest that the global transition away from polluting fossil fuels like coal, oil and gas will be at the center of attention in Antalya — once again. To date, there's been no consensus on whether and how to transition rapidly away from this main source of global warming.

Despite the setbacks, the world has made some progress thanks to the 2015 Paris Agreement.

David Victor, a climate expert at the University of California San Diego, pointed out that before then, the planet was hurtling toward an average temperature rise of between 3-3.5 C.

If current climate commitments are fully implemented, the latest UN projections show a rise of up to 2.6 C. It's a significant step forward, even though warming of that magnitude will still have worldwide consequences.

"There's no question that we could be doing more," noted Victor, though he cautioned against pinning too much on this year's summit.

All agreements at COP need to be unanimous, meaning individual states can quash any sweeping resolutions. Added to that challenge are the ongoing wars, trade conflicts and other economic problems swirling around this year's negotiations.

Industry observers note that "It's like a giant Christmas tree in which everybody's hung their different ornaments, and the tree is groaning and more ornaments are being put on it," mentioned Victor. "We have to look at it for what it is: It's a place where people talk about stuff.".

Instead of waiting for all COP member states to agree, Victor sees a better chance for change in what he called "clubs" — smaller alliances of governments and companies working together to advance actual solutions, whether it be in aviation, shipping or electromobility.

According to recent reports, "The Paris process is vital. It has to go forward," he told DW. "But all the work is going to be done in clubs.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

An example of this approach was last April's first ever International Conference on Transitioning Away from Fossil Fuels in Santa Marta, Colombia.

Colombia and the Netherlands invited representatives from 57 countries and key sectors to discuss ways to move the world away from coal, oil and gas, after an agreement on a similar strategy failed at the 2025 climate summit due to opposition from several oil-producing states.

With an eye to the ongoing trade conflicts and energy crisis, hosts Turkey and Australia have included green industrialization and the clean energy transition among their aims. One goal is to increase the share of electricity in global energy consumption to 35% by 2035, up from around 20% today.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

According to recent reports, A recent analysis by the International Energy Agency found accelerating electrification could cut fuel-importing countries' energy bills by more than $400 billion (€357 billion) by 2035, compared to 2025 levels. The idea could appeal to regions dependent on fossil fuel imports — among them Germany and the European Union.

Ahead of COP31, German Environment Minister Carsten Schneider said Germany and the EU wanted to spark newly introduced momentum in the "global phaseout of fossil fuels.".

It's wouldn't just be good for the climate, but a chance for many countries to boost their economies and reduce dependence on energy imports, added Schneider in a statement.

Oil-producing states like Saudi Arabia, however, aren't interested in deals that will undermine their business model. At recent UN climate conferences, they've repeatedly blocked any final agreements, including phaseout prepares.

Even China, despite its massive expansion of wind and solar energy over the last 20 years, could be against the idea. The economic superpower traditionally rejects any outside demands, proposals or interference concerning its national decisions on energy policy.

It has been revealed that every country in the world is affected by climate change, with loss and damage calculated in the hundreds of billions from heat, drought and storms. Worst hit are vulnerable countries in the Global South and island nations, who are at risk of disappearing as sea levels rise.

According to recent reports, that's where money comes into play, with developing countries calling for more support to protect their citizens from the harms of global warming. At the 2024 UN climate talks in Baku, Azerbaijan, industrialized nations agreed to free up at least $300 billion annually in climate financing by 2035.

But where exactly all those funds will come from remains hotly debated. At the same time, several major developed countries — most notably, the US — have cut their development aid.

The German government only paid out €4.7 billion from its 2025 budget for international climate financing, down from €6.1 billion in 2024.

"The level of financial support for developing countries today is far from what's needed," remarked Jan Kowalzig, a climate expert at Oxfam Germany.

Breaking financial promises like this comes at the expense of losing the trust of developing countries and, as a result, the diplomatic power which Germany and other industrialized nations rely on to shape policy to fight climate change.

Cosima Cassel, who focuses on climate diplomacy at the independent think tank E3G in Berlin, believes Turkey's push to turbocharge electrification during an oil crisis could be successful.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

For Cassel, a successful outcome at what are expected to be difficult negotiations in Antalya would reveal actual political will behind the grand agreements.

When it comes to electrification, that means taking the expansion of electricity grids and battery storage capacity seriously — not to mention removing the barriers to further electrification.

This article was originally written in German.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The 125th cap was no different to the first for Harry Kane, who has now been in the business of goal accumulation for so long that it is only at the landmark moments, that all of us are obliged to step back and take in the full scale of the work he has created.
  • Peter Shilton took 20 years to rack up his 125 caps, while for Kane it has been just 11 – and then there are the goals.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The 125th cap was no different to the first for Harry Kane, who has now been in the business of goal accumulation for so long that it is only at the landmark moments, that all of us are obliged to step back and take in the full scale of the work he has created.

Peter Shilton took 20 years to rack up his 125 caps, while for Kane it has been just 11 – and then there are the goals. Two more on Tuesday took him to 91 which means that only 12 other England players in history have more England caps than Kane has England goals. This unassuming man from Chingford, who looks like a mildly rebellious academic from the late 1950s, was at it again: the first-time strike, the back-post header. He has some misses across these 11 years, most infamously from the penalty spot against France at the Qatar World Cup almost four years ago, so, yes, there are some regrets too. But what sticks is the way he has taken his chances – again and again.

According to recent reports, ONE-TOUCH BRILLIANCE! ✨ Anderson, Rogers and Kane combine beautifully to double England's lead 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 Cap No. 125, goal No. 90 for the skipper 👏 https://t.co/otMcxlXyps.

Recent findings suggest that following his debut goal in 2015 against Lithuania, Kane has missed just 27 of the 152 England games since. He has added to the total like a great Test batsman patiently moving the scoreboard along. There was a bad run without goals in 2020 and before that in 2018. He scored only five in his first 17 caps and then scored 14 in his next 10. Against a very mediocre Czech Republic team this was classic late-era Kane, picking his moments and taking those chances with the usual absence of nerves. He was even substituted before the end.

Hall ➡️ Kane! The Newcastle fullback swings in the corner and it's the England captain who rises highest to head home 💥 https://t.co/5EhAcNZUqm.

In a recent development, afterwards at a Wembley press conference to mark the occasion, he invoked the cricket analogy himself on the question of scoring 100 England goals. “Being in the 90s, I try not to think about it too much, and it’s like I guess being a cricketer in the 90s. The more you think about the hundred… you don’t always get there.” There has still not been the elusive major trophy in the Kane England years but there has been success relative to the three decades that came before it. Semi-finals, finals – a good team if not a winning team.

At the centre of it has been a man around whom there has never been any scandal or, by the usual measure, much that might be described as spectacular. Rather it has been the scope of Kane’s career that is the most striking. The volume of the goals, of appearances, the capacity to be available – to play, to score – and the absolute quality of the player himself. He is determined to wring the very last drop out of his talent and usually refuses to acknowledge the prospect of the end, although there was a nod to it this time. “At some stage you know this opportunity isn’t going to be here,” he said. “I’m not going to be around forever, and I still hope that’s a long way away. But ultimately, of course, there’s times you’re tired or you’re injured, but I know I’ll miss it when it’s done. I try to always remind myself that and always try to make myself available.”.

One expects that when the end comes it will not be as rancorous as the final exit of Cristiano Ronaldo from Portugal, a drama playing out elsewhere. At some point, Kane will take his leave and it is likely to be as unassuming as the rest of it. He will be back at Wembley, injury permitting, for cap No 126 next month against Croatia. He talks like a different person to the one he was even five years ago – with a confidence and certainty about his place in the world. As opposed to the younger Kane, who seemed to regard everything outside his goalscoring tunnel vision with a general sense of bemusement.

“Availability,” he said, “is one of the biggest strengths you can have at this level for any coach.” He was keen to emphasise his “all-round leadership” too, “a lot of assets off the pitch”. He still measures himself in goals, of course, and perhaps there will be a Ballon d’Or too later this month – a prize that has eluded generations of England players before him who have won much more for their clubs than Kane has done. The good news for Kane is that his last England years will be spent in a very good England team – one which was on another level to its opposition on this occasion too.

No team in the top tier of the Nations League has scored more goals than England – 14 in the last four match days. Tuchel’s name was sung at Wembley and even if the World Cup semi-final collapse in Atlanta in July has not been entirely forgotten, the roughest edges have been taken off somewhat. Another great performance from Jude Bellingham and also from Morgan Rogers, in place of Bukayo Saka. Another dominant Elliot Anderson performance in midfield. They left Wembley to applause and a sense of optimism renewed.

England kept the ball with such authority, and none more so than Bellingham. Trent Alexander-Arnold came back at right-back. Myles Lewis-Skelly returned for another bite at a Wembley midfield job. As in Prague last week, there was a self-inflicted Czech calamity in the first half. The captain Vladimir Coufal appeared to lose his cool at the threat of the England attack all over the Czechs’ half. No other reason for this Premier League experienced full-back to fling himself at Kane’s cross and drill the ball past Newcastle goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek on 27 minutes.

Industry observers note that england lead! 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿⚽️ A great ball from Kane and a great finish from Coufal - unfortunately for the defender, it's in the wrong net...🫣 https://t.co/h54xQnunZM.

The second goal, on 40 minutes, was one for the ages. Anderson’s ball out to the right was met first time by Rogers for the cross and Kane ran into the space, as he has done so many times, to deliver a finish struck with customary assuredness. Bellingham almost flicked in Rogers’s cross on 56 minutes and from the corner that came after, Kane nodded in a header at the back post from Lewis Hall’s cross. All stated, the defending was woeful but there was nothing wrong with the finish.

Thomas Tuchel believes England have taken a step forward from their World Cup heartbreak over this international break and mentioned he was “honoured” to hear fans sing his name.

England finished their four Nations League games with a 3-0 win over Czech Republic, in which Harry Kane scored twice on his record-equalling 125th appearance.

It meant that Tuchel’s team have won three and lost one, against Spain, of their four games since the World Cup, after which the England head coach was heavily criticised for the semi-final defeat to Argentina.

Tuchel seems to have won the forgiveness of some England supporters, who sang his name at the start and the end of Tuesday’s game.

“It means a lot,” Tuchel stated. “It’s amazing to have a song. It’s the biggest honour. And I’m very happy and very honoured. They can be sure that I will give my absolute best to make our team win and play well.”.

According to recent reports, asked if he sensed a change in mood around his England team since the fall-out from the World Cup, Tuchel said: “I do and I think it’s necessary to move on. I think I can only repeat that we didn’t go out in the group stage. Sometimes it feels like that and we didn’t. As I said, our aim was always to progress, move forward and improve.”.

Tuchel snapped back at a reporter who questioned why he felt it necessary to repeat that England had not gone out in the group stage of the World Cup, claiming the criticism had felt a “little bit” too harsh.

But on whether England have shown they are a step ahead of where the team were at the World Cup during this international camp, Tuchel was far more positive and replied: “Of course and that’s what we have to do. That is our goal to constantly improve and develop.

In a recent development, “We had these experiences together and we had a big tournament together, and it was very positive. It’s necessary to move forward and improve, especially in sports. This is what we’re trying to do.

It has been revealed that “We adjusted some details in our structure and we didn’t compromise on the effort and the intensity, and on the togetherness of the team. The players who were with us in the World Cup took care of these standards and of the culture within the team, off the pitch and on the pitch, and I think that’s what you could see.”.

We played a very good match, very fluid and to put it into context it was the fourth match in 11 or 12 days. We dominated the whole match, had some good opportunities, scored some beautiful goals. Subs were strong. Very good performance again.

[Leading the way, Mr Kane] Of course. That’s what he does. I don’t take it for granted. It’s just exceptional, every single match. It’s just difficult to find fresh words to express it.

Training, attitude, cohesion, belief, of course [is why they’re stronger than ever].

Industry observers note that [Has the World Cup made England stronger?]  Of course, we got the first medal in 60 years. We didn’t go out in the group stage. We had a strong qualification, strong World Cup and strong camp. All four matches were on a high level. The camp throughout from the first day was on the highest level. You learn every day together. We grew stronger.

It has been revealed that I was happy that everyone who was in the camp was contributing. Everyone was on the pitch. Everyone revealed he was willing to give everything for the team and for the shirt. The guys who were with us for the World Cup set the standards high, made everyone feel welcome and everyone had a good camp.

He’s the best England player evert to wear the shirt and it’s an honour to play with him. And he’s only getting better.

It has been revealed that effective networking does not come naturally to everyone. Credit: sanjeri/Getty.

In a recent development, networking is not “random socializing”, says Nessa Carey. It’s a professional skill that can be learnt and developed.

Carey, a UK-based entrepreneur and consultant, explains in a six-minute video why scientists often struggle with networking, drawing on her own experiences while working in industry and academia.

According to recent reports, both Carey and Caroline Dunne, an academic careers coach based in the United Kingdom and Australia, describe how to identify good people to chat to, ask insightful opening questions and circulate effectively in a room packed with strangers. In her six-minute video, Dunne recommends arriving early and notes it is fine to leave an event before it formally ends.

The two videos formed part of a session on networking at Nature’s flagship Reframing Precision Medicine conference in London last month.

Published: 12:40 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 12:40 EST, 22 November 2026.

Tuur Rommens has urged his Rangers team-mates to use a breakneck run of three home games in eight days to build a platform from which to launch a real assault on the Premiership title.

Derek McInnes’ side play host to Aberdeen on Tuesday and then have Falkirk and Dundee United visiting – with Belgian left-back Rommens clear on the need to use the Ibrox atmosphere as a weapon.

‘At the away games, there’s a lot of fans, but at home there’s even more, so it gives an extra boost,’ he said.

‘I think, at home, we have to maintain our good run.

‘We’ll try to keep on winning these three games and then we’ll see from there. If you keep winning, you’ll be up there.

‘We’re back to Ibrox (on Tuesday) and it’s been a long time, but, yeah, it’s nice to play in front of our fans again.

Tuur Rommens (right) celebrates with match-winner Ryan Naderi at Fir Park.

Emmanuel Fernandez headed home the opener in Rangers' 2-1 victory at Motherwell.

‘I guess Aberdeen, it’s a difficult one, but we’ll try to keep on winning.’.

Rangers dug out a crucial 2-1 win at Motherwell on Saturday thanks to an 88th-minute Ryan Naderi winner and sit four points behind leaders Celtic with a game in hand.

Rommens believes the side’s ability to pull wins out of the fire and show they are willing to keep pushing right to the end of matches is helping build unity within the squad and with their followers.

‘Yeah, exactly,’ he said. ‘Also with the fans, when you score you feel a lot of emotions. You feel that they’re so happy, we’re so happy, so it gives us extra boost to go on Tuesday again and try to get a win.

According to recent reports, ‘I think the fanbase is unbelievable. It doesn’t feel like an away game because there are so many fans with us.

‘Especially for the fresh guys, that’s new. It’s the same for me. I’m not even here one year so I’m getting surprised every time that there are so many fans of Rangers when we’re playing outside.’.

Rommens also took time to lavish praise on Naderi and revealed what a deeply loved figure the Czech international has become within the dressing room.

Asked about the progress Naderi has made with his game in recent months, he replied: ‘It’s unbelievable.

‘You can always give the ball to him and he just keeps it.

In a recent development, ‘He’s very strong and I think he deserves all these goals that he gets. So yeah, I’m very happy for him.

‘He delivers, he scores a lot of goals, he gives assists, so everybody’s happy for him and he’s a good guy. Everybody loves him in the group.’.

'Never Again!': Holocaust remembrance under pressure

📅 08 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1293 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, young people pose inside a crematorium oven at the Buchenwald concentration camp memorial, laughing while they give the Nazi salute and take pictures of each other.
  • In a recent development, "Incidents like this have become more frequent in recent years.
  • Wagner is part of the curatorial team behind the exhibition "Never Again!
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, young people pose inside a crematorium oven at the Buchenwald concentration camp memorial, laughing while they give the Nazi salute and take pictures of each other. "In a sense, they're trophies to post on social media for them to boast about — breaking the ultimate taboo," Jens-Christian Wagner, director of the Buchenwald and Mittelbau-Dora Memorials Foundation, told DW.

In a recent development, "Incidents like this have become more frequent in recent years. We have seen memorial trees planted in honor of concentration camp victims cut down. When something like this happens — and it happens regularly — I find it particularly despicable because, because it ultimately kills these people a second time," added Wagner.

Wagner is part of the curatorial team behind the exhibition "Never Again! Against Forgetting the Crimes of the Nazi Regime" in Bonn's Bundeskunsthalle, or the Art and Exhibition Hall of the Federal Republic of Germany. Wagner stated Holocaust remembrance is under pressure, and the subject of intensifying attacks.

Critics have dismissed remembrance as a "cult of guilt" or "national masochism." With right-wing populism on the rise and historical revisionism becoming more common, Wagner worries about how Germany will remember the victims murdered by the Nazi regime. He is also concerned about the future of democracy. And soon, there will be no Holocaust survivors left to tell the true story of what happened.

This new exhibition tackles this concern head-on with numerous works of art and historical artifacts.

"I hope that perhaps even some people who don't already believe it's crucial to confront Nazi crimes will find their way to the exhibition," Wagner noted. Memorial sites also attract visitors who aren't necessarily convinced of the need to confront these parts of history. Many of them are students.

"Let's not kid ourselves: When a teacher notes 'We're going there,' it's always a mandatory visit," he noted.

For today's young people, the Nazi era seems like the distant past, Wagner explained. "When you tell them to remember something that their grandparents didn't even experience, it naturally feels like an emotional burden. They can practically see the finger being wagged at them, and that doesn't exactly encourage learning.".

Recent findings suggest that A two-hour lecture won't have much of an impact if pupils aren't even paying attention. Instead, Buchenwald organizes full-day programs that allow students to explore historical sources together and make sense of history for themselves.

In a recent development, the next step, Wagner said, is to show young people that this chapter of history isn't closed. Visitors are encouraged to make connections between the past and current events like migration, for example.

It has been revealed that "For the longest time, people have been discussing migration almost exclusively in terms of threats to public safety and crime. This broadly marginalizes certain groups — a mechanism that also worked for National Socialism," he noted.

Eva Umlauf, 83, knows firsthand what it means to experience exclusion in its most extreme form. She is a patron of the Bonn exhibition.

According to recent reports, in November 1944, Umlauf was just 2 years old when she, her pregnant mother and her father were deported by the Nazis from the Novaky labor camp in Slovakia to Auschwitz-Birkenau, the notorious Nazi concentration and extermination camp. She was saved from the gas chambers by mere days; the Nazis stopped using the chambers as the Red Army advanced, hoping to hide evidence of their crimes.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Sources indicate that the camp was liberated on January 27, 1945. Three months later, Umlauf's sister Nora was born. But her father, her mother's siblings and her grandparents were all murdered. Eva barely survived herself. She suffered from tuberculosis, rickets and whooping cough, as well as edema caused by starvation. "Forget about the child. She won't survive," a doctor told her mother. But he was wrong.

Her mother returned to what was then Czechoslovakia with her two daughters, settling in Trencin. Eva Umlauf has no conscious memories of Auschwitz, but she carries her family's trauma deep within her.

Recent findings suggest that her mother never talked about what happened. Even so, Eva knew from an early age that she was a survivor. Her family rarely mentioned the camp by name, but one sentence came up again and again: "They stayed there." Eva knew that meant "they" were dead. And then, there was the number tattooed onto her arm: A26959.

According to recent reports, her mother taught her daughters not to draw attention to their Jewish identity — antisemitism was widespread throughout Czechoslovakia at the time. The small family managed to avoid harassment.

It has been revealed that eva Umlauf wanted to become a pediatrician, so she studied medicine. In the 1960s, she met her future husband, Jakob, who had also survived the Holocaust. He was an architect, active in Munich's Jewish community. They married in 1966, and she moved to Germany. She could hardly have imagined that she would one day live in the country of the perpetrators. "I don't hate Germans," she noted. "But I cannot forgive. How can you forgive the deaths of 6 million people?".

It wasn't until much later that she first spoke publicly about the horrors of her early childhood. In 2011, she delivered a commemorative speech in Auschwitz on the anniversary of the camp's liberation. Since 2025, she has served as chair of the International Auschwitz Committee. A heart attack in 2014 motivated her to write her first book. "I was in intensive care. I thought to myself: If I get out of here healthy, I'll write a book.".

Her memoir, "The Number on Your Forearm is Blue Like Your Eyes," was first released in 2016. The English translation followed in 2024. Since its publication, hardly a day has passed without someone asking Eva Umlauf to share her story.

She is appalled by the disrespectful behavior of young people at former concentration camps and by growing ignorance about the Holocaust. Sometimes, people even ask if she's too old to have a tattoo. But she also recalls a young man on the Munich subway who noticed the number on her arm and told her: "I want to apologize to you for what my ancestors did to you.".

It has been revealed that umlauf never imagined that antisemitism would once again become so widespread in Europe and the United States. Nor did she expect the rise of Germany's far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party.

"I go into schools. I'm so overwhelmed by the number of requests asking for my availability. And yet, the AfD is growing faster than I can reach students. It makes me think all this work is for nothing," she told DW.

It has been revealed that germany must never again fall under a right-wing dictatorship, she stressed. "'Never again' sounds nice, but all I can say is: It's happening again! Wouldn't 'Here We Go Again: Never Again' make a good title for the exhibition?".

Recent findings suggest that she also shared her message to young people in the exhibition catalog, "Never Again": "You are not responsible for the crimes of your grandparents and great-grandparents. But you are responsible for the future. […] You are the generation that will shape our world. Make it a place where everyone can grow up safely, regardless of their background, faith or skin color.".

She continues: "You don't have to be perfect. You just have to stay alert. Take care of your country.".

Sources indicate that the exhibition "Never Again! Against Forgetting the Crimes of the Nazi Regime" in the Bundeskunsthalle in Bonn runs through May 2, 2027.

This article was originally written in German.

In a recent development, right, where were we? Three weeks on from the fifth round of Premier League fixtures in which the champions Arsenal were beaten 3-0 by Brighton and todays’ visitors, Leeds United, who remain unbeaten, drew in a tepid goalless fixture with Crystal Palace, we finally get to the sixth. As worrying as the result was at the Amex, Arsenal still created a shedload of chances and last season they were the one club that battered Leeds in both games – first early in the season when they were playing four at the back and before Dominic Calvert-Lewin, a late signing, was fully fit, and then later after they had successfully switched to a “base formation” of three centre-backs and the tactical flexibility that allowed.

Recent findings suggest that it was a 5-0 tanking in August and 4-0 in January, so to say Leeds travel to a ground at which they have never won more in hope than expectation would be as true as much as it is hackneyed. Adding to a sense of foreboding and thanks to Opta’s excellent Jonny Cooper, we also have to take into account the fact that Leeds, floodlight kings, have not won a Premier League match kicking off before 3pm since August 2022 and have not won a match in London since beating Brentford in May that year to save themselves from relegation. However, they do boast the division’s best defensive record – three goals conceded – and the No1 ranked goalkeeper in James Trafford who has a save percentage of 87. For all the sense of doom, though, Leeds have become a very good side and their spine – Trafford–Muharemovic–Ampadu–Calvert-Lewin marries steel and class.

Recent findings suggest that roma continues their pursuit of a winger. Tony D’Amico is working to please Gian Piero Gasperini, who has been calling for a reinforcement in that position for several months to add new options to the defense.

Several names are on the table, but in the last few hours a newly introduced lead seems to be gaining traction: Samuel Lino.

According to Brazilian portal RTI Esporte, the Giallorossi are pursuing the player seriously, so much so that they have already initiated contact with his entourage and submitted an official €45 million offer to Flamengo.

The Brazilian club, recently crowned champions of the league, hasn’t closed the door on a possible transfer but would only be willing to part with one of their key players if they receive a particularly high offer.

Samuel Lino was one of Flamengo’s key players this season, finishing with 13 goals and 9 assists. Roma is waiting to see if there is enough room to move the deal forward.

Svilar: “De Rossi changed my life, Gasperini taught us how to win.”

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (620 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Romapress

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • After more than a month’s absence, Mile Svilar returned to the pitch, defending Roma’s goal in the match against Parma at the Tardini.
  • The Giallorossi number 99 then gave an interview to Cronache di Spogliatoio, discussing, among other topics, his relationship with De Rossi and Gasperini.
  • The night against Feyenoord in the Europa League in 2024: “That night was the real start of my professional career.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After more than a month’s absence, Mile Svilar returned to the pitch, defending Roma’s goal in the match against Parma at the Tardini.

The Giallorossi number 99 then gave an interview to Cronache di Spogliatoio, discussing, among other topics, his relationship with De Rossi and Gasperini.

The night against Feyenoord in the Europa League in 2024: “That night was the real start of my professional career. From there, everything changed. In those three games—the two against Feyenoord and the one against Frosinone—I started to be a professional. I once told my wife that many goalkeepers start out as second or third-choice, then start playing well due to injuries and start like that. Up until that point, it had happened to me many times in my early years at Benfica, a little less so at Roma, but I never had the feeling inside that it was the right time. “.

“had the feeling that it could never happen to me. But that week, I had it, I felt that my moment had come. A feeling you can’t explain. I felt that something would happen like it does to the others. I knew it was the moment. I never noted it, but I knew it. I had a different adrenaline rush, the feeling of being important.”.

“In every job, you need someone who believes in you. And De Rossi was the person who believed in me, who gave me the push. He put me on the field, he had the power to change something, and Daniele changed my life, the life of my family.”.

Industry observers note that “The week before his arrival, I played with AC Milan, but it ended a bit badly. Then we had Verona at home, and during the week I already knew I wouldn’t play. I wasn’t surprised. But he was the first person who called me into his office and mentioned, ‘Look, Mile, I chose not to let you play and let Rui play. But in training, I saw something really interesting, so train because your time will come soon.’ For the first time, someone wanted to explain to me before the match and tell me I wouldn’t play. I immediately felt that he would be different for me.”.

It has been revealed that “De Rossi’s dismissal hurt. I felt bad. He was someone who changed everything for me, in football and therefore in life. I will be grateful to him for the rest of my life.”.

Sources indicate that “Last year was spectacular. But there were some low points, and many around us no longer believed in it. But when you keep doing, keep doing, like we’re doing with the coach, it’s something I’ve never seen.”.

“Gasperini’s biggest contribution? The mentality. The physical and tactical work the boys put in because it’s a different way of playing. There’s a winning mentality, which is what we needed because this club truly has everything it takes to do well.”.

According to recent reports, “Our objectives? It’s hard to say right now. As everyone can see, we’re doing really well. The tactical and physical work is putting a lot of us ahead. Maybe we were a little behind or something like that before, but now we’re moving up.”.
