📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AWAY FAN GUIDE: BRENTFORD v EVERTON.

Stadium: Gtech Community Stadium.

Address: Lionel Road South, Brentford, TW8 0RU.

Matchday Updates: Brentford recommend their social accounts, as follows:.

Visiting fans are seated in the East Stand, using turnstiles H, G (Accessible entrance) and F.

Turnstiles will open 90 minutes prior to kick off and fans are advised to arrive early.

Please note that fans visiting the Gtech should expect a robust searching process as part of efforts to ensure a safe environment for all supporters. This may include the searches of bags and other personal items carried by supporters. Privacy can be requested when searching personal items, please speak to a member of staff who can help.

Fans without tickets for this fixture are urged not to travel to the stadium.

Everton Travel Stewards will be on hand to help supporters with any complications. For updates from Merseyside Police, follow @MerPolEFC on X.

Pubs around the stadium generally welcome both home and away fans.

The Pilot or The Gunnersbury are recommended for fans travelling from Gunnersbury.

The Express Tavern, One Over the Ait, The Bell & Crown, The Steam Packet and City Barge are the closest pubs to the stadium.

The Rose and Crown, The Greyhound, The Coach & Horses and The Botanist are the closest to Kew Green and typically all welcome away fans.

A map of pub locations can be found HERE.

This fixture is sold out and supporters should not travel unless they have a valid match ticket.

Supporters in the visitors’ section will have received a paper ticket for this game by post.

If any supporter has not received their ticket, please contact Everton's fan services at 0151 556 1878 or direct message the team on X @efc_fanservices.

If you need any further matchday assistance, you can visit the stadium box office, or speak to a matchday steward located near to turnstile entrances.

Any persons under the age of 14 must be accompanied by a responsible adult.

A summary of travel options is set out below.

There are eight stations located within a 20-minute walking radius of the stadium, so if you are planning to travel either by train or tube to the stadium, please consider the following:.

The nearest station, Kew Bridge, has one South Western Railway train every 15 minutes on matchday Saturdays (and up to four trains per hour on Sundays), with trains every 15 minutes on weekdays (up to 10pm, then every 30 minutes until the last train).

It has been revealed that trains to the stadium from central London are from Waterloo station. Gunnersbury station is the nearest station offering both the District Line underground and London Overground connections.

Fans should note that during busy times, there may be a long wait to access the station. For any supporters that require step-free public transport options, please contact accessibility@brentfordfc.com so that we can discuss and agree the best option for you.

Brentford station, the nearest step-free station, is a 24-minute walk.

Gunnersbury (nearest) 16 min walk.

The following routes serve the stadium: 237, 267, 65, H91 & 391.

Fans are advised to check for the latest information about bus routes at tfl.gov.uk or via other travel management apps.

It has been revealed that all London Style ‘Black Cabs’ are wheelchair accessible and can provide a suitable alternative to the bus or car. There is no formal drop-off point on site at the stadium. If you have difficulty walking from the surrounding area, please contact up at accessibility@brentfordfc.com and we will try to assist you.

Industry observers note that fans can make use of matchday car parking via JustPark HERE. Spaces must be pre-booked.

Ultra Low Emission Zone (ULEZ) has expanded across all London boroughs. You can check the roads that are inside the ULEZ and whether your vehicle meets the emission standards HERE. (Vehicles that don’t meet emission standards will be charged £12.50 per day to drive inside the expanded ULEZ area and fines are charged for those that do not pay this tariff).

Controlled Parking Zones will be in operation in residential streets near the stadium so you should not plan to park on nearby streets.

It has been revealed that four disabled parking spaces are reserved for away supporters. These are located very near to the away entrance on Capital Interchange Way and available on a first come, first served basis. Contact accessibility@brentfordfc.com for details.

Sources indicate that blue badge parking spaces are also available at Our Lady & St John’s RC Primary School where a mini-bus shuttle is available for those that need it. These spaces must be pre-booked. The shuttle will run every 30 minutes up until kick-off. If you require a shuttle timetable or more information, please contact accessbility@brentfordfc.com.

Industry observers note that the mini-bus shuttle will drop blue badge holders from Our Lady & St John’s RC Primary School to the Bees Superstore. If you require a wheelchair pick up when departing from the shuttle bus at the Bees Superstore, please email accessibility@brentfordfc.com detailing your expected arrival time.

Please note: the mini-bus shuttle can only transport foldable wheelchairs and there are a few steps to negotiate to access the shuttle bus.

All official away coaches must park on Capital Interchange Way, TW8 0EX which is adjacent to the away end turnstiles. If you have an accessible coach travelling or require any additional information, all contact should be directed to the Supporter Liaison Officer at supporterservices@brentfordfc.com.

Away fans will be discouraged from using Kew Bridge station post-match (see travel options, below) but any that do choose to use this station will have to walk round from Capital Interchange Way and up Lionel Road South to join the same queuing system as for home supporters.

There are two food and drink kiosks available in the away end, with a range of options on offer (including vegetarian and vegan options) as well as both alcoholic and soft drinks. All food counters have been designed at a height to make them fully accessible for fans in wheelchairs.

Industry observers note that payments: The stadium is fully cashless. All major contactless debit and credit cards will be accepted. Mobile and wearable payment options including Apple Pay and Google Pay are also supported.

Please note that fans visiting the Gtech should expect a robust searching process as part of efforts to ensure a safe environment for all supporters. This will include searches of bags and other personal items carried by supporters. Privacy can be requested when searching personal items - please speak to a member of staff who can help.

Brentford strongly recommends that fans do not bring bags with them to the stadium.

Bags that exceed the permitted dimensions of 34 cm (H) x 24 cm (W) x 11 cm (D) will not be permitted into the stadium, including suitcases. These dimensions are slightly larger than the height and width of an A4 sheet of paper.

Please note that bags cannot be folded to meet the size limit. Stewards will have apparatus to measure bag sizes. Exemptions to the bag policy are available to fans with medical and accessibility requirements. We can also allow exemptions for parents of small children who need provisions such as nappies and bottles with them inside the stadium. If you need an exemption, you should request one as soon as possible by contacting accessibility@brentfordfc.com and providing evidence and information as to why you need a larger bag.

Fans with oversized bags that are not permitted into the stadium will be directed to the bag storage facility at the Bees Superstore, located next to the A4/M4.

Prams and buggies can also be stored here.

Bag storage will cost £5 per item for most bags and £10 per item for the largest bags and suitcases. Any profits from the bag storage will be donated to Brentford FC Community Sports Trust.

A comprehensive Access Guide is available HERE.

All queries should be directed to Disability Access Officer, Connor Bagenal via the dedicated mailbox at accessibility@brentfordfc.com.

Wheelchair viewing: There are 14 wheelchair spaces available for visiting supporters.

In a recent development, on arrival, you will find a passenger lift that provides access from Thomas Layton Way down to ground level, where the turnstiles are located. Turnstile G is the designated accessible entrance and on the concourse you will have access to a large passenger lift serving the elevated accessible seating areas.

Audio Descriptive commentary: Headsets and transmitters are available where required and should be booked in advance by emailing us at accessibility@brentfordfc.com.

Away supporters will be able to collect their booked headset from the away end turnstile once into the ground. Please speak to the stewards, who will have the supporters' name and you will be issued with the headset. Please return the headset to a steward when exiting the stadium.

It has been revealed that accessible toilets: There are plenty of high-quality toilet facilities located throughout the stadium, including an ambulant accessible toilet with additional space in each toilet block, as well as separate accessible toilets, all of which are clearly signposted. Within the away end, there are also three accessible toilets available, with one located on the lower concourse and two on the upper concourse. Each accessible toilet is clearly signposted and fitted with a RADAR lock. Supervising stewards carry RADAR keys in case a supporter with access requirements does not have their own.

Recent findings suggest that changing Places: There are two Changing Places Toilets within the stadium, one on the second floor of the South Stand and one in the main concourse of the North Stand within the Family Area. Supporters in the West or East Stands (including the away end) requiring access to these Changing Places Toilets should ask a steward who will escort them. The Changing Place Toilets include a large space for both the user and carer to move freely within the room, accessible toilet, hoist, movable changing bed, privacy screen along with seating for other owners.

Assistance Animals: Brentford welcome assistance dogs at the stadium. Please inform them in advance at accessiblity@brentfordfc.com.

Smoking, or the use of e-cigarettes is not permitted anywhere across the stadium site.

Everton has a zero-tolerance approach to discriminatory behaviour or language at matches and while travelling to and from fixtures.

The Club’s All Together Now campaign promotes equality, diversity and a football family for everyone.

If you witness or experience any behaviour in the stadium which you believe  falls below the standard of behaviour that you would expect, we encourage you to report it as soon as possible. Please report what you see or experience to any matchday steward, or on WhatsApp* text +442038330327 with details of the incident and our Operations team will be notified. Alternatively, you can email report@brentfordfc.com at any time.

Everton supporters can also report discrimination confidentially at: reportit@evertonfc.com.

Please consider fellow Evertonians, particularly on concourses.

Behaviour such as throwing beer may result in ejection. More serious incidents may result in arrest and stadium bans.

Recent findings suggest that everton works with the relevant authorities to identify those responsible for unacceptable behaviour. CCTV can be used as evidence after an incident, even where an individual was not detained on matchday.

Everton does not condone pyrotechnics under any circumstances.

Possession or use may result in Club sanctions, arrest, criminal conviction and a football banning order.

Entering the playing surface without permission is a criminal offence.

Those responsible risk Club sanctions, football bans and criminal consequences which can affect employment, education and international travel.

Please enjoy your matchday and stay safe.

Thank you for your continued support and for helping protect Everton Football Club’s reputation while making the matchday experience enjoyable for everyone.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • We’ve put together a Premier League ‘substantial six’ mini league for the 2026-27 season, tracking the results between Arsenal, Liverpool, Manchester City, Manchester United, Chelsea and Tottenham.
  • It has been revealed that the concept of the ‘major six’ feels increasingly outdated.
  • The last time all six clubs actually finished in the top six was back in 2021-22, and it doesn’t appear likely to happen again soon, with the likes of Brentford and Brighton threatening to upset the apple cart this time around.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We’ve put together a Premier League ‘substantial six’ mini league for the 2026-27 season, tracking the results between Arsenal, Liverpool, Manchester City, Manchester United, Chelsea and Tottenham.

It has been revealed that the concept of the ‘major six’ feels increasingly outdated. Newcastle United and Aston Villa have challenged the established order in recent years, while Man United, Chelsea and Tottenham have all endured miserable campaigns miles off challenging at the top.

The last time all six clubs actually finished in the top six was back in 2021-22, and it doesn’t appear likely to happen again soon, with the likes of Brentford and Brighton threatening to upset the apple cart this time around.

In a recent development, but the distinction still holds some weight. These six clubs remain among the Premier League’s biggest spenders in terms of wages and transfer fees, and their financial muscle means they’re rarely far from the conversation. For now, we’ll stick with the traditional definition.

In a recent development, last season, Manchester United topped our 2025-26 ‘big six’ mini league, despite finishing well behind champions Arsenal in the actual table. The Red Devils took 22 points from their 10 matches against their fellow heavyweights, including doubles over Liverpool and Chelsea, with Michael Carrick landing the job on a permanent basis in large part due to some statement victories.

It’s been a different story this season. United have lost all four of their ‘major six’ encounters, most recently suffering a humiliating 4-0 defeat to Liverpool at Anfield. That result proved to be Michael Carrick’s final game in charge, with Mauricio Pochettino appointed as his successor.

Industry observers note that unfortunately for the new boss, his first match could hardly have gone much worse, with United comprehensively beaten on Merseyside. Pochettino has a huge job on his hands, with his side having conceded eight goals in four heavyweight encounters without managing a single victory.

According to recent reports, manchester City, meanwhile, have made a flying start in these fixtures. Enzo Maresca’s men followed up their controversial derby victory by thrashing Liverpool 3-0 at Anfield, an emphatic statement victory that struck a defiant tone following the news of the Premier League finding them guilty of the vast majority of their 115 charges. That stands in stark contrast to their subsequent run of form against teams lower down the table, with dropped points against Aston Villa, Nottingham Forest and Fulham.

Recent findings suggest that tottenham have also made an encouraging start, taking four points from their first two outings. A late equaliser earned them a draw at Old Trafford before they registered a particularly impressive 2-0 victory away to Chelsea. Things finally seem to be headed in the right direction under Roberto De Zerbi, with a rare victory at Stamford Bridge potentially a turning point.

Xabi Alonso’s Chelsea have endured a mixed start, losing 2-1 at Arsenal and suffering a disappointing 2-0 home defeat to Tottenham before bouncing back with a 2-0 victory over Manchester United.

Liverpool have had a mixed start to their substantial-six fixtures, losing 3-0 to Manchester City and failing to score against Arsenal. But they produced a statement response against Manchester United, running out 4-0 winners at Anfield in a result that gives Andoni Iraola’s project some momentum.

Mikel Arteta’s champions, meanwhile, have maintained their perfect record with a statement 1-0 victory at Anfield, their first league win there since September 2012 and the first under the current boss.

Kai Havertz’s early goal proved decisive, with the Gunners producing something of a Mourinho-esque defensive masterclass to keep Liverpool at arm’s length. Six points from six against Chelsea and Liverpool is an excellent return, and it reveals their big-game mettle after their excellent display in the Community Shield curtain-raiser against Manchester City.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Newcastle United suffered a painful, chastening defeat, comprehensively beaten by Coventry City in a performance that should send a shudder of fear through Tyneside.
  • It was a dreadful night for the visitors, who conceded four goals for the second successive away game.
  • Newcastle are too easy to create chances against and there is not much that gets you excited when they attack.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Newcastle United suffered a painful, chastening defeat, comprehensively beaten by Coventry City in a performance that should send a shudder of fear through Tyneside.

It was a dreadful night for the visitors, who conceded four goals for the second successive away game. The manner in which they fell apart was damning. Whatever the supposed style of play, it is not good to watch: long balls are pumped forward for short strikers to chase or compete for in the air against far taller centre-backs. Away from home, it is becoming ineffective.

Newcastle are too easy to create chances against and there is not much that gets you excited when they attack.

Matthias Jaissle’s side did create chances against Coventry, but are not clinical and do not inspire confidence they can be with the players they have. Defensively, they escaped earlier in the season, but are now being exposed and punished. “Not good enough in both boxes,” was Jaissle’s blunt verdict. “To concede eight goals in two away games is not good enough.”.

Industry observers note that matthias Jaissle on this evening's defeat at the Coventry Building Society Arena. https://t.co/216NW6Laz8.

Newcastle’s misery was in stark contrast to the joyous celebrations from Coventry. This was a thoroughly deserved first home win of the season for Frank Lampard’s side.

Industry observers note that “It was an outstanding performance,” the manager stated. “We knew we would have to suffer at times against a team like Newcastle. But we were really good at the basics, winning the second balls, winning the duels, those moments are critical. It’s not always about pretty patterns, it’s about work ethic.”.

It has been revealed that the win lifts Coventry level on points with Manchester United and will give them fresh confidence at this level. This could be the start of something special for them.

Recent findings suggest that as for Newcastle, this raises uncomfortable questions about their summer recruitment, with so many expensive players on the bench or playing badly. It also means people will query whether Jaissle’s implementation of “vertical football” is working. The fact Lampard talked so openly about winning the duels to set up the win will anger the German.

Jaissle can point to two bad misses from one of the newly introduced arrivals, Matias Fernandez-Pardo, a £51m buy from Lille, in the first half. But his team are too easy to play through and the defence is an accident waiting to happen.

It has been revealed that even after Sven Botman’s stunning strike offered them a way back into the game, they capitulated at the back as Lewis Hall – who was off colour all evening – and Joelinton’s mistakes gift-wrapped a third for Ellis Simms. A fourth followed for Stephen Mfuni.

Sources indicate that ellis Simms off the bench with a significant impact! 💥 https://t.co/XynFVxwERV.

You can get a sense of what sort of mode a team are in within the first few passages of play and Newcastle were not sharp or precise. It was sloppy.

That was certainly true of goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek, who was off his line in no-man’s land trying to snuff out a through ball that he was not going to get. He stood up to deflect it away, but then rashly chased after it, diving at full stretch at the feet of Coventry’s Sidiki Cherif and failing to get the ball. Jack Rudoni coolly sent the Czech goalkeeper the wrong way from the spot.

Newcastle had been awful in their last away game at Leeds, another 4-1 thrashing, and there were many of the same faults on display.

It was not a good first half for Fernandez-Pardo up top. They are mystified in Belgium why he believes he is a centre-forward rather than a winger and he did not do himself any favours here. Newcastle’s best move of the game resulted in Lewis Miley playing in Jacob Murphy down the left. His cutback was perfect for Fernandez-Pardo to sweep home at the near post but instead of trying to make contact, he dummied it, thinking Harvey Barnes was better placed. He was not. It was a baffling piece of centre-forward play.

It had been the easiest 40 minutes Lampard’s side have had since they were promoted, but Newcastle still should have scored before the break.

Industry observers note that nico González spotted the run of Fernandez-Pardo through the middle. He wriggled clear of Bobby Thomas and sat down goalkeeper Carl Rushworth, but the Coventry centre-back got back to block his shot.

There was a half-hearted attempt to close Cherif down from Yoane Wissa and then a shot that somehow went through a crowd of three Newcastle defenders, including the legs of Botman, and nestled in the bottom corner.

Significant in Japan. It is a term that modern beat combos use for overseas success. It applies equally to Clyde FC, purveyors of association football for 150 years, who now have a Japanese owner. Or two or three.

‘We have 1,100 owners in 59 countries,’ a club official tells me as the supporters’ lounge in Fresh Douglas Park fills with fans of both football and Bleed From Within, a heavy metal group.

This fusion has been created by the band’s sponsorship of Clyde’s third strip. It is the latest example of the club’s innovative thinking.

‘Clyde Worldwide is a key part, we want to spread the word of the club all over,’ says chief executive David Henderson of the ownership scheme. ‘We would like these fans to become actively involved. It costs 60 quid a year but we don’t just want them to sit on the sidelines. We could use their skills and expertise.’.

Indeed, one American owner has applied to join the board and will soon be up for election.

The owners come from the USA, Indonesia, Nigeria, Costa Rica and the Faroe Islands among many other different locations.

Clyde have partnered with Scottish metalcore band Bleed From Within.

Band members Craig Gowans, Steven Jones and lead singer Scott Kennedy.

Sources indicate that ‘We don’t have a community in the sense that we don’t have a permanent home of our own,’ says Henderson. ‘So this is a way to create excitement and a bit of a buzz. I am a believer that if you get the basics right at a club then everything falls into place.’.

He adds: ‘We still have to find a home. That is the key point. We are still pursuing Stepford in Glasgow but we are awaiting the council on that. But we are stressing that we will be a positive for any venue in that we will bring people, bring investment, we will build things up. But we do the best we can while we are here.’.

Recent findings suggest that it was an hour before kick-off. An hour earlier, a punter walked into the fan zone carrying the news that the Bleed From Within shirt had sold out.

In a recent development, ‘We ordered 500 from the manufacturers thinking that would be enough. But in the first couple of hours of the sale online we knew we had to think about re-ordering more,’ indicates Henderson. ‘After 24 hours we had sold four times the amount of our home kit,’ he says. Other merchandise has sped across the world as a result of Clyde Worldwide. The global match stream was offered at a discount to celebrate Bleed From Within day. It was a bargain with seven goals in a smashing match.

Clyde, The Movie, may be the sequel to Clyde, the heavy metal musical. ‘I love football and I love history and was looking at the stories here outside of Celtic and Rangers,’ states Bryan Wendland, a filmmaker from Newly introduced York who now lives in Glasgow.

‘This is a historic Glasgow team who have not played in Glasgow since the eighties. The club trying to find a way back into the city was an interesting story that would have a lot of branches to follow.’.

Industry observers note that wendland, 35, who has made short films in his homeland, aims for the Clyde project to be a feature film or series. It is a long-term project and ideally it needs Clyde to find a home in Glasgow.

It has been revealed that the exile from Glasgow has fascinated Wendland. ‘I have been surprised at how many people have deep roots in the fandom of this club,’ he indicates.

In a recent development, he believed that the decades away from Glasgow would have destroyed that lineage of support. However, the strand of family support is still strong. ‘That is both surprising and moving,’ says Wendland.

‘I love generational stories,’ he claims. ‘I support teams in America because my father supported them.’.

Unwittingly, he is sitting in the fan zone across from one of the best examples of this syndrome.

Stephen Muckalt, a retired driver, is a third generation Bully Wee fan. ‘I have only missed seven games in 45 years,’ he says. ‘I first went to Shawfield in 1971 when I was seven. The family is from Rutherglen so I followed my grandfather and father to Shawfield.

Industry observers note that ‘The demise of Oatlands and Dalmarnock in terms of population has historically hit the club hard but there is still a good core who come from Rutherglen. I watch them every week.’.

Clyde are flying high in League Two and sport their new kit.

According to recent reports, ‘Stupidity,’ he states with a laugh. ‘No, it’s a love of the club. I have been kitman, in charge of the ball boys, I ran a school of football, so I have done my stint.’.

Recent findings suggest that he points out that the crucial problem is finding a home for the club. ‘We are nomads and we need somewhere to settle,’ he states. ‘If this was in Rutherglen, it would be ideal.’.

A father and daughter have made the trip from Paisley, but not primarily to watch the football. Ian Donald and Jane Donald are fans of Bleed From Within.

‘I teach her good music,’ notes Ian. ‘We have seen them a few times. She likes to stand at the front of the stage and I am a bit back. We have brought along a Saltire for the group to autograph. We love their style of music but we also love the fact that they are Scottish.’.

It has been revealed that he adds: ‘This is the first time I have been at Newly introduced Douglas Park. I support Rangers and my daughter supports Celtic.’.

Music has the power to cross all divides.

Recent findings suggest that there is a mystery. ‘I just don’t know,’ states Steven Jones, when asked how the name of Bleed From Within came about. It was there when he joined the band 10 years ago.

The band meet supporters before Clyde take on Stirling Albion.

And sign autographs for Clyde fans that believe a return to League One is within reach.

He is, though, sure of the band’s love of football.

‘We all come from south Lanarkshire and love the game,’ he says. ‘We had a band strip made for Scotland in the World and that went so well we were open to this. This sponsorship supports Scottish football so we are all for it.’.

The link with Clyde is geographical. ‘We rehearsed out of a building in Dalmarnock for 10 or 11 years so we kind of contracted an affection for the club there,’ he says.

Three of the band walk into the fan zone to be greeted by applause and requests for autographs.

‘This is a bit of a strange gig for us,’ indicates Jones. ‘We are not here to play music so that makes it unusual for us but the afternoon has been great.’.

Recent findings suggest that the weirdest gig for the band in his eyes was one in eastern Czechoslovakia, as it then was. ‘We had to drive hours to this place and there were only 25 people there. The hall was like the scene of a vampire movie but it went well.’.

The highlight was supporting Slipknot on their 2023 tour of the UK. ‘We used to say when things were not going great in the early days that we would look back on it all and laugh when we were supporting Slipknot. And then it happened.’.

The world has a way of producing such surprises. Like Clyde shirts selling out and owners throughout the world watching a Scottish League Two match in a variety of international time zones.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Chelsea, Tottenham Hotspur, Manchester United, Liverpool, Manchester City and Arsenal are all sitting in vastly contrasting places when you compare their wage bill rankings to their league positions after the first 11 games of the 2026-27 Premier League season.
  • Of course, it’s still early in the season.
  • Still, there are already some big, eye-catching differences between wage outlay and performance.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chelsea, Tottenham Hotspur, Manchester United, Liverpool, Manchester City and Arsenal are all sitting in vastly contrasting places when you compare their wage bill rankings to their league positions after the first 11 games of the 2026-27 Premier League season.

Of course, it’s still early in the season. Eleven matches can tell us only so much about how the season will eventually play out, and the table is still taking shape.

Still, there are already some big, eye-catching differences between wage outlay and performance.

Brighton lead the way. They are second in the Premier League despite having the 15th-highest wage bill, which stands at just £51million. That is a remarkable +13 difference between their league position and wage ranking.

In a recent development, leeds United are next best in that regard. They are sixth while ranking 14th for wages, with a £53million annual bill, giving them a +8 difference. Hull City are similarly overachieving, sitting 11th despite having the 19th-highest wage bill at just £16million. Their +8 difference is another remarkable return for a newly-promoted side.

Sources indicate that brentford are also joint third. They sit 10th while ranking 17th for wages, with an annual bill of just £49million. That’s a +7 difference.

Bournemouth are next, sitting fifth while ranking 11th for wages, with an annual wage bill of £63million. That’s a +6 difference, level with Everton, who are seventh despite having the 12th-highest wage bill.

The traditional powerhouses have produced a mixed bag. Arsenal are top while having the third-highest wage bill in the division, at £154million. That puts them two places ahead of their wage position, while Manchester City sit third in the league and second in the wage rankings.

Chelsea are eighth with the seventh-highest wage bill, £97million, while top spenders Liverpool are fourth. The Reds have the highest wage bill in the Premier League at £177million but sit three places below that ranking.

According to recent reports, the other ‘Major Six’ underachievers are not hard to spot. Manchester United are 19th with the fourth-highest wage bill of £152million, while Tottenham are ninth despite having the fifth-highest at £138million.

Villa are also slightly off the pace. They are 12th despite having the sixth-highest wage bill, with £98million going on salaries. That puts them six places below their wage ranking.

According to recent reports, we’ve ranked every Premier League club by the gap between their league position and wage-bill ranking, from the biggest overperformers to the biggest underperformers. Keep an eye on this one, as we’ll be keeping it updated as the season progresses.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • England may have edged a step closer to booking their place at next summer’s Women’s World Cup but they do not yet look like a team who can win it.
  • This two-legged qualifying play-off with Greece was always going to be somewhat academic.
  • Industry observers note that the goals flowed more freely in the second half, but Greece deservedly found the net themselves and are not yet out of the tie.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

England may have edged a step closer to booking their place at next summer’s Women’s World Cup but they do not yet look like a team who can win it.

This two-legged qualifying play-off with Greece was always going to be somewhat academic. Greece are ranked 58th in the world and have never qualified for a major tournament. But they could – and should – have taken the lead before England eventually broke the deadlock through Georgia Stanway just before half-time.

Industry observers note that the goals flowed more freely in the second half, but Greece deservedly found the net themselves and are not yet out of the tie. There is every chance of the Lionesses winning the second leg in Leicester on Tuesday more comfortably, but not being able to put teams to the sword is exactly why they ended up in the play-offs in the first place.

According to recent reports, the best teams are ruthless and unforgiving – and England did not display those traits here. They snatched at chances, and several players were guilty of firing wide. There were also defensive problems. Greece got in behind England’s back line too often and the goal they scored was far too easy for them.

“I think we made it [the game] a bit harder,” England manager Sarina Wiegman said. “Greece were very well prepared. They were very well organised and well disciplined. Of course I’m happy with the 3-1, I’m not happy with the one.

“We could have scored more goals, we should have. The final stage, the final pass needs to be better. I think we were a little bit in moments really good on the ball and in other moments not so good, and we could have made better decisions too. Lots of things to take from today.

“Sometimes we played really well, sometimes we were a bit sloppy, so sometimes we were a bit frustrated and I think that’s what you saw.”.

Avoid defeat in the second leg and England will play the winners of Ukraine v Slovakia. Ukraine, whom the Lionesses beat 6-1 and 3-0 earlier in their campaign, have a 3-1 lead from their first leg. Perhaps the pedestrian nature of this game was partly because it felt inevitable England would win. They did enough to get over the line but still lacked a clinical edge.

It has been revealed that it had been four months since they were thrashed 4-0 by Spain, a defeat which relegated them to the play-offs instead of automatic qualification. They had won every other game in their group before that capitulation, but with Spain topping the group on goal difference, England only had themselves to blame for not scoring more goals in their other fixtures. Breaking down ultra-defensive teams has long been an glitch for this Wiegman side and they knew that was what they would be facing in this double-header against Greece.

It did not help that many of Wiegman’s players have been struggling for form in the Women’s Super League this season. Wiegman was also without the ever-reliable Lucy Bronze, who dropped out of the squad on Thursday because of injury. That meant Maya Le Tissier was handed a start at right-back while Laura Blindkilde Brown was preferred to Jess Park in the No 10 position.

Recent findings suggest that greece were far more open than many would have expected, with several gaps in their defence for England to exploit. They also created problems for themselves by insisting on playing out from the back.

It has been revealed that england thought they had taken the lead in style when goalkeeper Fafailia Petaloti gave the ball away needlessly. Lauren James took advantage of Petaloti being off her line and produced a tremendous lob from 25 yards out. But the forward was offside when she picked up the ball and the goal was ruled out by VAR.

The excellent Kathryn Batte has run the rule over potential alternatives to Lucy Bronze.

The 35-year-old right-back is out injured, but Ella Toone was called up in her place, rather than a direct replacement.

“Bronze, who is two appearances away from reaching 150 caps for her country, has picked up an injury and returned to Chelsea for treatment,” Batte writes.

“The Lionesses will be missing one of their most reliable players for the matches on Friday and Tuesday, but it gives Sarina Wiegman an opportunity to look at potential replacements for the future.

According to recent reports, “Bronze, who has been an integral member of the team throughout Wiegman’s reign, turns 35 later this month. While she will be expected to be the first-choice right-back should England qualify for next year’s World Cup in Brazil, the lack of a recognised back-up has been an ongoing problem.”.

Sarina Wiegman revealed that while dropping Toone was a difficult decision, the midfielder’s reaction left a lasting impression on the coaching staff.

“When I gave her the call, of course that was a hard call, but she took that straight away,” Wiegman noted. “Of course she was very disappointed, but the first thing she did was say: ‘OK, I’m going to get back, I’m going to do that.’”Wiegman was particularly pleased with how Toone handled herself both on the pitch and in front of the media before her late recall.

It has been revealed that “That answer in the game, also the way she spoke about it, I thought that was really good,” the head coach added. “And then getting everything ready, I think that really impressed me. Well done, I would say.”.

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Greece vs England in the first leg of the 2027 Women’s World Cup play-offs.

Sources indicate that the Lionesses kick off the two-legged tie tonight looking to secure a solid advantage ahead of Tuesday’s return tie at Leicester’s King Power Stadium. Although they finished level on points with group winners Spain, England’s goal difference sent them into the play-off path, setting up a first-ever senior meeting against a Greek side ranked 55 places below them in the FIFA rankings.

All eyes are on Sarina Wiegman’s selection choices following a turbulent week of squad news. The manager originally raised eyebrows last month by dropping Ella Toone and Chloe Kelly, stating bluntly that “the levels weren’t what I expect from them on the pitch.”.

Toone rapidly accepted the setback. Speaking after starting in Manchester United’s victory over Liverpool, the midfielder insisted: “It’s about me now. I’ve got to keep working hard and use it as fuel to come back even better.”.

That opportunity arrived sooner than expected. An injury sustained by right-back Lucy Bronze - described by Wiegman as “really small” - forced the defender to return to Chelsea for assessment. Wiegman immediately turned to Toone, who flew directly to Greece from Spain, where she had been running her own self-directed training block during the international window.

With 69 caps and 24 international goals to her name - including crucial strikes in the Euro 2022 final and the 2023 World Cup semi-final - Toone brings proven substantial-match experience back into the setup at a critical moment.

We will bring you all the build-up, confirmed team news, and live play-by-play coverage throughout the evening.

Breaking: Iran war oil shock drives dip in global emissions, study indicates

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Global carbon emissions are set to slightly drop this year, a fresh study suggests, largely as a result of high energy prices in the wake of the US war on Iran and the disruption of supply through the Strait of Hormuz.
  • In a recent development, emissions from oil, gas and coal are the main drivers of climate change.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Global carbon emissions are set to slightly drop this year, a fresh study suggests, largely as a result of high energy prices in the wake of the US war on Iran and the disruption of supply through the Strait of Hormuz.

In a recent development, emissions from oil, gas and coal are the main drivers of climate change. While over the past decade, these emissions have risen by 0.9% per year, they are expected to drop by 0.4% in 2026.

"It's downwards, which sounds good, but this is largely driven by the war in Iran, what's happened in the Strait of Hormuz," stated the study's co-author Glen Peters, a scientist at the CICERO Center for International Climate Research in Norway.

"So in a way, a little bit of good news, but for the wrong reasons.".

The study was released while global leaders are meeting in Turkey for the United Nations' COP31 climate conference.

In a recent development, the study published by international research group the Global Carbon Project found that oil emissions dropped by 1.9% in 2026, while natural gas fell by 0.3%. Coal emissions however continued to rise, by around 0.6%.

"A drop in emissions in ‌one year is not a peak unless it ‌is driven ​by structural change," Peters cautioned.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

A structural change would mean that emissions would slowly rise to a peak and then slowly decline afterward, indicating a long term trend. That's not what happened though, Peters noted. "What we see this year is [that] oil emissions are going up and then suddenly, bang, down 2%.".

It is the third time in recent years that global carbon pollution has dropped. The previous declines were during the global economic crisis in 2009 and during the COVID pandemic in 2020. In each of those cases, emissions went back up once global economies recovered.

According to recent reports, while the geopolitical shocks of the past year have been the driving factors behind the temporary emissions reversal, there has also been a rise in renewable energy contributing to the data. So while solar panels, wind farms and electric vehicles did make a difference, they were just not enough to cut emissions by themselves.

"The long-term answer remains the rapid deployment of clean energy technologies," according to co-author of the study, Pierre Friedlingstein, of the Global Carbon Budget Office at the University.

According to recent reports, and even though emissions from fossil fuels dropped slightly, overall global carbon dioxide emissions still went up by about 1%, the study warns. The overall rise is because of land use changes like deforestation and peat fires, which increased too fast to be offset by the slight decrease in fossil fuel burning.

Malen d’Or? Forgotten Villa player on Mbappe’s tail in European Golden Boot race

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (728 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Planetfootball

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that it’s just getting a bit silly now.
  • Yep, that’s nearly as many as Inter’s Marcus Thuram and Como’s Anastasios Douvikas – the pair on 13 in the same timeframe – put together.
  • In fact, no player in Europe’s top five leagues can match him.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that it’s just getting a bit silly now. Since Aston Villa sold Donyell Malen to Roma in January, the most any other player in Serie A has scored is 13 goals. Malen has scored 25.

Yep, that’s nearly as many as Inter’s Marcus Thuram and Como’s Anastasios Douvikas – the pair on 13 in the same timeframe – put together.

In fact, no player in Europe’s top five leagues can match him. The leader in that time in the Premier League is Erling Haaland with 16; it’s Raphinha in La Liga with 21; Harry Kane in the Bundesliga with 20; and Esteban Lepaul in Ligue 1 with 19.

It’s the sheer consistency that makes Malen’s impact at Roma so impressive. His drive and determination have helped him showcase what he wanted to all along: he’s an elite goalscorer.

In a recent development, he was in a mean mood on Saturday, scoring four past Parma. His first saw him expertly guide the ball beyond his marker after a cross before slotting home, with the rest all showing his clinical nature in the box.

Sources indicate that this is just what Malen does for Roma. He’s found a system where he’s the central figure, playing in his preferred position that he never got a chance to consistently with Villa. He’s backed himself ever since the move and he’s been good for his word.

His efforts against Parma gave him his third hat-trick for Roma, but he went one better and became their first player to score four goals in a Serie A game for almost 25 years.

Donyell Malen hit FOUR past Parma 😮‍💨#ParmaRoma #UNROSSOALLAVIOLENZA pic.twitter.com/gulnLRKO2J.

— Lega Serie A (@SerieA_EN) November 22, 2026.

If you weren’t already, it’s time to start taking him seriously in any debates about the best strikers in Europe. Sure, he doesn’t quite have the same potency for the Netherlands, so you could argue he’s a system player, but when he scores as often as he does in that system, it’s got to count for something.

Sure enough, Malen is becoming one to watch in the race for the European Golden Shoe. Only Raphinha and Kylian Mbappe have scored more than him in Europe’s top five leagues so far, and he’s only one goal behind the latter.

Industry observers note that mbappe won the European Golden Shoe two years ago, in between Harry Kane’s two triumphs. It would take a herculean effort for Kane to retain the accolade due to his current injury, so someone like Malen’s eyes should be lighting up.

Industry observers note that he really is hot on the heels of Mbappe right now. You’d imagine the Frenchman will stay the course, while current leader Raphinha has been sensational so far since being converted into a striker himself at Barcelona, but will it last?

Some might ask similar questions about Malen, but he’s been doing this for nearly a year now. There might have been doubts over his ability to carry this form from last season into this one, and he’s made a mockery of them.

Sources indicate that carry on at this rate, and the Serie A golden boot that he came close to capturing last season – despite having half as much time to aim for it as his rivals – could be his. Beyond that, the European Golden Shoe, or even a Ballon d’Or nomination (for the 30-man shortlist, at least) might not be out of reach.

It has been revealed that this Roma side have produced the best start to a season in the modern era in terms of goals scored at this stage. Of course, Malen has been front and centre of those efforts.

His latest Instagram post featured music in the background – a song named after him where the singer muses: “Maybe now I only love Bobby Malen.” (Oh, yeah, they call him Bobby over there – it’s a long story).

Just a classic case of a footballer finding a club he fits in at like a glove, and loving life. File that under things you love to see. Unless, perhaps, you’re a Villa fan. Or maybe even a Golden Shoe-hunting Mbappe….

There will be some games where Mikel Arteta has no choice but to tweak the XI, rest some tired legs and give his second-choice attackers the chance – although given the option he may wish to pick the same team every week.

Lille are considering legal ⁠action after defender Tiago Santos suffered a serious knee injury following an “uncontrolled and dangerous” tackle in Saturday’s match ‌against Le Havre.

Santos, 24, suffered a ruptured anterior cruciate ligament and meniscal tear in his right knee and was carried off the pitch on a stretcher after being tackled by Le Havre midfielder Amir Richardson during the first half of Lille’s 1-0 victory.

Lille mentioned the ‌tackle merited ‌a red card ⁠and that they had asked the league’s governing body (LFP) to refer the matter to its disciplinary committee. The club are also seeking an explanation of ⁠the video review process undertaken by match officials.

Industry observers note that arsenal pay tribute to one of the club’s greatest custodians this evening following the news of Ken Friar’s death aged 92. Friar worked in various roles at the club across more than 70 years, and a bridge from Drayton Park to Emirates Stadium is named in his honour.

A statue at the end of the bridge is a nod to the chance meeting the 11-year-old Friar had with Arsenal manager George Allison in 1945, while playing football outside Highbury with his friends.

Sources indicate that as Sam Dean wrote earlier today, finishing the story: “Allison was so impressed by Friar’s enthusiasm that he told him to report to his office at 9am the next day. Friar did as he was instructed and his reward was a job offer: he became a messenger at the stadium on match days. He was paid 12 and a half pence per week.”.

Friar was a long-serving member of the Arsenal board, before stepping back in 2020 and becoming life president.

Arsenal’s players will wear black armbands.

A post shared by Sam Dean (@samjdean_tel).

After signing his new Arsenal contract last week, Mikel Arteta described May’s Champions League final defeat as “poison in his veins,” and last season’s campaign demonstrated the benefits of finishing top of the league phase.

Arsenal enjoyed home second legs all the way through to the final after winning eight from eight, and in a 50:50 draw they fell into a considerably kinder bracket.

Sometimes it can be hard to gauge the importance of these league-phase matches, but Arteta will strive for another perfect record to give Arsenal the best possible chance of going deep in the competition again.

Fixtures against Bayern Munich and Real Madrid are likely to determine whether Arsenal finish in the top two, but there is still a job to be done against Lille this evening.

Arsenal have played against 10 different French opponents in European competition but have never faced Lille, who are managed by Davide Ancelotti, son of five-time Champions League winner Carlo.

Lille sell their best players every summer. After finishing third in Ligue 1 last season they lost Ayyoub Bouaddi and Matias Fernandez-Pardo to Manchester City and Newcastle United for a combined £130m. They have claimed 10 points from their first five league games of the season and led Paris St-Germain 2-0 before being pegged back in stoppage time.

Industry observers note that leading the line for Lille is 40-year-old Olivier Giroud, who scored 105 Arsenal goals in 235 appearances between 2012 and 2018. After leaving the Emirates, Giroud went on to score against Arsenal for Chelsea in the 2019 Europa League final, but he can still expect a warm reception.

Arsenal’s home record in the Champions League has been formidable since they returned to the competition under Arteta in 2023. They have won all 11 home group-stage or league-phase matches, conceding just three goals (two of those were shipped against Kairat Almaty in a dead rubber).

Arteta’s scope for rotation has been reduced by injuries to Piero Hincapie and Martin Zubimendi, but tonight’s game should offer Eberechi Eze and Viktor Gyokeres a chance to impress, while Jurrien Timber needs minutes to build his fitness.

#140251. Why malnutrition can go unnoticed, and what that means for our health

Why malnutrition can go unnoticed, and what that means for our health

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1009 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Some 50,000 deaths can be attributed to malnutrition in Germany each year, according to the German Society for Nutritional Medicine (DGEM).
  • The problem is that malnutrition often doesn't become apparent until the consequences are already severe.
  • "In most cases, you don't notice anything at first," noted Matthias Pirlich, a nutritional expert and internal medicine specialist, who once served as DGEM vice president.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Some 50,000 deaths can be attributed to malnutrition in Germany each year, according to the German Society for Nutritional Medicine (DGEM).

The problem is that malnutrition often doesn't become apparent until the consequences are already severe.

"In most cases, you don't notice anything at first," noted Matthias Pirlich, a nutritional expert and internal medicine specialist, who once served as DGEM vice president. "You could have a severe vitamin D deficiency for months before any symptoms appear at all. The same applies for vitamin B12. By the time symptoms appear, such as nerve damage, it's already too late.".

Recent findings suggest that A long-term B12 deficiency can damage the spinal cord, leading to numbness in the limbs, muscle weakness or even paralysis. Less common deficiency-related brain damage can cause memory loss and mental health issues.

All B vitamins play an important role in metabolism, blood formation and healthy nerve function.

In a recent development, vitamins, along with various minerals such as calcium, magnesium, iron, iodine and zinc, are classed as micronutrients. The body needs to source them from food, as it cannot produce them itself. Our bodies also need macronutrients like carbohydrates, carbohydrates, protein and fats that provide us with energy.

Sources indicate that if the body consumes less food than it needs to maintain all bodily functions over a prolonged period of time, then this is known as undernutrition. A recent World Food Organization (FAO) report estimates that approximately 645 million people worldwide suffer from chronic undernutrition.

Sources indicate that malnutrition, on the other hand, occurs when we consume enough calories but lack certain macronutrients or micronutrients in our food. This, too, can make one sick over time and even prove fatal. About 2 billion people worldwide suffer from this so-called hidden hunger, most of them in the Global South. That noted, even some people in industrialized nations lack important micronutrients in their nutrition.

It has been revealed that one study, for instance, found that just under three-quarters of the US population did not meet the recommended daily intake of vitamin D between 2007 and 2010, with more than two-thirds falling short of the recommended amount of vitamin E. And in Germany, about one-third of the population suffered from vitamin D deficiency in 2017, according to the German Nutrition Society. Such deficiency can cause bone, joint and muscle pain. It may also lead to an increased risk of falls and bone fractures.

In a recent development, about one-third of Germans also had an insufficient intake of iodine, a trace element that is indispensable for the production of thyroid hormones. Iodine deficiency can therefore disrupt normal thyroid function. Not only that — during pregnancy, a baby's brain and nervous system can only properly develop with an adequate supply of iodine.

The cultivation of agricultural produce with partially long shelf life or high yields has in some cases caused a decrease in the micronutrient content of fruits, vegetables and grains. Whether this drop in micronutrients is impacting human health, however, is a matter of debate.

Malnutrition can result from an unbalanced diet that, while filling and providing energy, lacks essential micronutrients. Examples of such empty calories include fast food and highly processed foods, as well as white bread and white rice.

Poverty is often the reason for such an unbalanced diet, for example when people in the Global South can only afford to buy staples such as flour or rice.

Another study found that in Germany, households at risk of poverty are more likely to consume foods that are low in nutrients and high in calories.

Sources indicate that depression is also associated with an increased risk of nutrient deficiency. "People often lose their appetite, and when they neglect their self-care, they may end up eating a very unbalanced diet," Pirlich told DW. His research demonstrates that older adults and people who live alone often develop malnutrition, too. The risk also increases the more medications a person takes.

Sources indicate that many diseases result in the body being less efficient at absorbing or utilizing nutrients through the intestines. This applies to people with inflammatory or chronic disease, such as Crohn's disease, celiac disease, liver disease and cancer.

The DGEM estimates that some 30% of all patients receiving inpatient care in Germany are affected by or at risk of malnutrition. Yet health insurance data shows that only about 1% of patients are screened and treated for nutrient deficiencies.

Often, patients' malnutrition worsens during their hospital stay. The consequences can be serious, potentially causing additional complications, delayed recuperation, longer hospital stays and even increased mortality rates. This results in higher healthcare expenditure, amounting to billions each year.

It has been revealed that german policymakers and medical associations are therefore developing a plan to better screen for and treat malnutrition in hospitals. The road map will be ready by 2027 and copy the Dutch approach in the sense that all patients are checked for nutritional deficiencies upon hospital admission.

Pirlich wants to see such screenings for at-risk groups in outpatient clinics, too: "This includes all those with chronic and serious illnesses and, above all, older adults.".

To prevent poverty-related malnutrition, Pirlich suggests increased access to healthy food, offering free school meals as an example.

In a recent development, the nutritional expert recommends eating a diet that is varied and largely plant-based. "Secondary plant compounds have a very positive effect, and if you eat a highly diverse diet, you consume many different foods that are [nutritionally] beneficial," noted Pirlich.

There's a simple rule of thumb: The more colorful your food, the better.

Also, cook vegetables as gently as possible, because overheating and keeping them warm for too long destroys their vitamins. Long storage periods also lead to vitamin loss, so it makes sense to go for seasonal and regional foods in particular.

But even when ensuring a healthy and balanced diet, some people still develop a nutrient deficiency. A blood test can provide clarity, and dietary supplements may help make up for the deficiency.

This article was originally written in German.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Michael Carrick had urged his Manchester United players to come out and fight. But nobody could have imagined quite how Lisandro Martínez would interpret that message.

By the end of an extraordinary evening in Madrid, where United went 1-0 down inside a minute and never recovered against Atlético Madrid, Martínez had blown the lid off any pretence of all being well at the club as he launched a lacerating assault on the club’s executives.

United had come into this getting battered from all sides and when Pablo Barrios put Atlético ahead, Jamie Carragher’s pre-match assessment about how things could get “very messy, very promptly” for all involved at Old Trafford must have been ringing in the ears of the travelling supporters.

It has been revealed that ATLETICO ARE AHEAD IN JUST 53 SECONDS! ⚡️ A nightmare start for United at the Metropolitano Stadium 😬 https://t.co/TdOwoXxopn.

Industry observers note that they certainly know how to make life difficult for themselves. Leny Yoro’s 74th-minute red card pretty much ended hopes of them taking something from the game.

Ademola Lookman scored Atlético’s second soon after and Carrick was staring at another defeat. And so they now move on to a big game at Leeds on Sunday. This was not the result Carrick would have wanted – and that is before what happened off the pitch.

Ademola Lookman PUNISHES a 10-man Man United 💥 https://t.co/GHKYIHGhNC.

Another defeat intensified the pressure on Carrick but Martínez left nobody under any illusions that he felt the finger should be pointed not simply at another manager or the players, but the hierarchy above him.

It was extraordinary to see a player speaking out so publicly in this fashion against his own bosses.

But Martínez pulled no punches, even going as far as singling out Jason Wilcox, the director of football, as he criticised the club’s summer transfer business and effectively accused the club of failing Carrick and the players in the window.

To what extent Martínez’s comments mirror the views of the wider dressing room is unclear, but you have to wonder where Carrick and United go from here.

On the one hand, Martínez was providing a show of support for his manager by attacking the people above him. At the same time, he has presented Carrick with a disciplinary problem to address.

Lisandro Martínez did NOT hold back after United's loss to Atletico 😬👀 https://t.co/OGo25Pzd30.

And United have enough troubles as it is without a senior member of Carrick’s dressing room turning so squarely against the club’s power brokers.

Martínez was probably only giving voice to what many fans have been saying since an underwhelming transfer window closed with more questions than answers. But for a player to talk in such blunt, excoriating terms resonated more loudly than anything a supporter or United’s most caustic critic could say.

The message was simple: you can sack all the managers you want but until you pull together a squad worthy of United’s name and give the man at the helm the tools to compete, the club will struggle to escape this cycle of mediocrity.

In a recent development, no one can reasonably argue United’s window was a success. They went into it with the hopes of landing Elliot Anderson and other premium midfielders but ended up going for numbers over proven quality or pedigree. Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba were not a trio of signings anyone expected at the start of summer, not even the club itself.

There were glaring issues to address in defence, not least at left-back, and at centre-forward but a quality alternative to Luke Shaw never materialised and no back-up was signed for Benjamin Sesko, who was missing for four months with a shin injury that has since resurfaced and which could keep him out for a while yet.

Industry observers note that having done so well to lead United to third and take them back into the Champions League, Carrick would have expected further backing than he got in the summer. Ever the company man, he has been too polite to criticise that lack of investment. But the cat is out of the bag now Martínez has had his say.

Industry observers note that it now places the spotlight on Wilcox. United head to Elland Road on Sunday and that was the scene of Rúben Amorim’s final meltdown as manager. Two days after he blew up in a meeting with Wilcox at United’s Carrington training base, Amorim took aim at the director of football and others at the club, demanding they “do their job” and repeatedly declaring that he had come to Old Trafford to “be the manager, not to be the coach”.

It is remarkable to think that, 10 months on, United head back to Leeds with just as many questions as there were back then.

United’s worst start to a league season for 40 years has ensured Carrick is already under pressure, but Martínez is very much of the view that it is no longer enough for the manager and the players to keep carrying the can and that the credibility and suitability of those who recruit the players and make the decisions must now be called into question.

Industry observers note that that Martínez picked this game to speak out was interesting. United, lost, yes, and the manner of Atlético’s opening goal from Barrios after 53 seconds was shocking. But United at least went down fighting on this occasion and had fashioned enough good chances to at least draw level before Yoro’s harsh 74th-minute red card swung a delicately poised match decisively in Atlético’s favour.

Lookman made it 2-0 soon after, but Atlético, having looked like they would run all over United in those opening 10 minutes, were made to work hard for their victory.

Industry observers note that united cannot keep shooting themselves in the foot like they did in the first minute. Carrick had gone with a three-man midfield to shore things up and made his team more comfortable and yet they were opened up in double quick time by two passes through the middle.

Still, you only needed to look across at United’s opponents to appreciate how chaotic it had become at Old Trafford.

Diego Simeone’s reign at Atlético covers a period stretching two years longer than the post-Ferguson era and in many ways his teams have represented everything United have not been in that time: well constructed and thought through, unified, stable, organised, hungry, aggressive, uncompromising and with a flash of devilment.

If United were not in crisis before this, they are now.

Lisandro Martínez did NOT hold back after United's loss to Atletico 😬👀 https://t.co/OGo25Pzd30.

And then the red card which I thought was a really poor one. It’s difficult after that. Disappointed that with the chances we had we didn’t [get] more [out of the game].

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the Champions League tie between Atlético Madrid and Manchester United from the Metropolitano. The two sides had contrasting fortunes in their opening fixtures in this competition, Man Utd beating Azerbaijan’s Sabah 4-0 at Old Trafford a month ago while Atléti were defeated by Liverpool who came back from 1-0 down to win 2-1.

But domestically it is the other way round – Michael Carrick’s side have made the club’s worst start in the league for 40 years with one win, three draws and two defeats and have been knocked out of the League Cup. Those of us who watch them regularly – purely because of occupational obligations in this instance – have been surprised by how poor they have been. The results have been bad but the performances even worse.

According to recent reports, they seem to lack players who can play on the front foot, who have the athletic dynamism required in this league and too many self-indulgent forward players who either can’t be bothered to help out their team-mates or cannot concentrate long enough to do so. Spooked by their lack of pace in defence and midfield, they are hidebound by caution, dropping ever deeper, ever more reliant on counter-attacking despite the blatant disconnect between the front four and back six. If they drift through this match and Sunday’s trip to Elland Road, Carrick may join the long list of Ineos-driven managerial mis-steps.

In a recent development, atlético have won six of eight in La Liga and have been defeated only once. They are five points behind Barcelona in second and have score 18 goals and let in eight, which may seem a curious thing to include in a preview but it is done to emphasise that many fans’ perception of Diego Simeone’s team are out of date. Back in the days of Diego Godín, Gabi, Juanfran et all, six wins a draw and a defeat would have had goals for of about 10 and goals against of maybe three.

Sources indicate that simeone is a martinet about attitude not systems or styles and his team have evolved, with the World Cup-winner Alex Baena, who has scored four goals so far, driving them on. He has reintegrated Julián Alvarez, too, after his brazen attempt to force a move to Barcelona so incensed Atléti fans that it seemed they would drive him out of the club. Simeone refused to let Alvarez get his own way and he is now buckling down. Ten years ago Simeone would have bitten his head off.

According to recent reports, the one surviving veteran in the squad from that first of El Cholo’s Liga winning sides and the two Champions League finals, victory in which would represent Simeone’s crowning achievement, is the midfielder Koke. Remarkably, if he features today, the 34-year-old midfielder will be making his 750th first-team appearance as an Atlético player.

There was no grand gesture as Bradley Barcola walked back to the bench, just a high-five from Andoni Iraola and some of Liverpool’s coaching staff.

Sources indicate that it was a similar situation as he left the stadium. Hood up, jacket zipped, baseball cap pulled on tightly, he politely turned down all requests to talk in English. “Not good enough,” he mentioned with a smile, but that was the only thing that had not been up to standard.

Recent findings suggest that the giveaway here was what he held in his right hand – the match ball. On it were the signatures of Liverpool’s squad, congratulating him on a momentous performance that had arrived right on cue.

If you are going end a barren spell, you do not want to just turn on the taps but burst the dam, and that is precisely what Barcola did on a wild night in Austria. He needed one goal to get his Liverpool career up and running, he ended up scoring three.

Iraola had noted he was not concerned about Barcola’s numbers when Liverpool arrived in Linz, even if no goals and no assists since his £123m move from Paris St-Germain had caused debate, but those numbers look infinitely better now after his first senior hat-trick.

Bradley Barcola's first ever senior hat-trick ⚽️ He's been unplayable 🔥 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/UMhUDmGPo9.

According to recent reports, “I’m really happy for Bradley, because you were asking me yesterday about him, not making the numbers,” Iraola smiled. “Also Florian [Wirtz], and I think both of them played really, really well. They made a difference. Bradley apart from the hat-trick I thought he was a threat.

According to recent reports, “He was always one-on-one, certainly in behind and he helped us a lot to control the game, finding the pockets. I am happy for both of them, yes. For their confidence for sure, it’s very good. I think they feel now that we trust them a lot. It’s going to be very good for them.”.

Barcola should have had the stage to himself on an evening when Liverpool were so obviously better than LASK in Linz but it will have frustrated Iraola immensely that his team scoring six times was tarnished by three daft goals being given up in the final 25 minutes.

We can look at the late switch off in due course but the only place to begin is with Barcola, who looked ready for business as early as the eighth minute when his first touch was a cushioned back heel, taking possession by crossing one leg behind the other, and how he seized his moment.

Liverpool had already taken the lead when Ronald Araújo rose powerfully to head in a Kostas Tsimikas corner but, two minutes after, the Barcola show began, a confident right-footed shot being swept past Lukas Jungwirth from 10 yards after some good build-up play from Rio Ngumoha and Lewis Koumas.

Liverpool needed Barcola to deliver as much as the player himself needed to prove a little point and there is absolutely nothing wrong with having a cause to light a fire. Like a batsman who has been waiting nervously to get off the mark, soon the France international began playing his shots.

A young Liverpool team has been selected to face Linz – the third youngest, according to Opta, that the club have fielded in the Champions League – and Andoni Iraola is being mindful of players such as Virgil van Dijk and Alexis Mac Allister being overburdened ahead of Saturday’s trip to Brentford.

One novice who certainly deserves his starting spot is Trey Nyoni, the England Under-21 international has impressed in the opportunities he has been given so far this year. Watch out for his calmness on the ball and the efficiency with which he uses it.

He should get more chances in the next 10 days, as it is difficult to see Dominik Szoboszlai being ready at least until the home match against Brighton on Sunday week.

Asked about Liverpool’s youthful team, Iraola stated: “For me Trey [Nyoni], [Lewis] Koumas and Rio [Ngumoha] are young players coming in from the academy but they are first team players.

It has been revealed that as Dominic King writes in this piece: “Barcola had no control over the price that Richard Hughes, Liverpool’s former sporting director, brokered with Paris St-Germain for his release. But something he can control is public perception and, with no goals or assists so far, opinions are starting to form.”.

Of the five Premier League teams in the Champions League this season, Liverpool have the friendliest league-phase fixtures and they can secure back-to-back wins against Austrian side LASK in this evening’s early kick off.

Having already vanquished one of their pot one opponents by beating Atletico Madrid at Anfield, Andoni Iraola’s team really should be targeting one of the top spots.

They travel to Linz without some key players, though. Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai missed the defeat by Manchester City and remain sidelined, while Hugo Ekitike is a long-term absentee.

There were positive aspects to Liverpool’s performance against City, but they collapsed like a deck of cards after Ryan Gravenberch’s harsh second yellow card.

Tonight’s game is one they should dominate, and it is a presentable opportunity for Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola to kick-start their seasons and respond to the recent criticism of their performances. Iraola hopes to have a stronger squad to choose from at the weekend, when Liverpool face a stringent test at Brentford. This is the second of nine matches in 28 days for Liverpool.

Recent findings suggest that “You don’t have a lot of time to train,” stated Iraola. “You try to prepare the games now a lot of times just with the videos and the tactics boards, just a little bit outside. You have to prioritise the freshness of the players.

“Especially now we are playing four games in 10 days, it’s keeping all the legs, all the energy in the games.

LASK are currently third in the Austrian league, but booked their place in this season’s Champions League proper with a remarkable comeback from 4-0 down on aggregate against Celtic.

They have injury problems of their own to contend with George Bello and Moses Usor limping off in the weekend’s defeat by league leaders Rapid Wien and Ramiz Harakate tearing his anterior cruciate ligament in July.

They do play on a grass pitch at the Raiffeisen Arena though Kasper Schmeichel, the former Celtic goalkeeper who was working as a TV pundit for the game, was critical of the playing surface.
